Finance Director Roy Danziger submitted copy of a letter for informational purposes only from Miami -Dade County Property Appraiser's Office to the Mayor and Council of the 2016 Assessment Roll Estimate which will be approximately $1,972,000.00. The Town will begin receiving the money in November or December 2016. Councilperson Digiacomo stated that she received phone calls from residents that use the shopping trip twice a week. They want to know if there was a way that they do not have to switch busses every time they go on the shopping trip. She would like clarification. Lizmari Valido stated that the shopping route is controlled by the Miami -Dade County Citizens Independent Transportation Trust (CITT) Program and the residents have to be picked up at designated locations and anyone can ride on the bus, not just Medley residents. The Town cannot pick up the residents at their houses or take them back to their houses. Councilperson Digiacomo stated that the Town picks them up at their houses for music night. Lizmari stated that that is a different program; it has nothing to do with the CITT Program. Councilperson Digiacomo asked how much money does the Town receive from CITT a year. segs.head: (1) This Ordinance amends the M-1 Zoning District Regulations to provide for a Solid Waste Facilities Overlay District as a separate sub -district within the M-1 category.
segs.text: (1) This Ordinance amends the M-1 Zoning District Regulations to provide for a Solid Waste Facilities Overlay District as a separate sub -district within the M-1 category.

segs.head: (2) It defines Solid Waste as Class I Landfill, Class III Landfill, materials recovery facility, waste -to -energy facility, and recovered materials processing facility, which have received required Florida DEP and locally required permits.
segs.text: (2) It defines Solid Waste as Class I Landfill, Class III Landfill, materials recovery facility, waste -to -energy facility, and recovered materials processing facility, which have received required Florida DEP and locally required permits. Composting facilities are excluded.

segs.head: (3) Creates a new Section 62.91 of the Town Zoning Code establishing a special exception process for the application of the Overlay District to a specific property.
segs.text: (3) Creates a new Section 62.91 of the Town Zoning Code establishing a special exception process for the application of the Overlay District to a specific property. Special exception process applies to all types of Solid Waste Facilities.

segs.head: (4) Application for special exception must be filed and may be granted by Town Council after public notice and hearing.
segs.text: (4) Application for special exception must be filed and may be granted by Town Council after public notice and hearing. The Town council may grant a special exception upon findings that the application complies with detailed standards of review and criteria established in the Ordinance.

segs.head: (5) Provides for permitted and accessory uses within the Overlay District.
segs.text: (5) Provides for permitted and accessory uses within the Overlay District.

segs.head: (6) Special exceptions may be granted to: (a) permit uses described in the Ordinance, and (b) authorize deviations from the terms of the Town's Zoning Ordinances relating to setback and frontage requirements, height limitations, lot size restrictions, yard and building requirements, subdivision regulations, and other requirements unrelated to use, except for the buffer requirements established in the Ordinance.
segs.text: (6) Special exceptions may be granted to: (a) permit uses described in the Ordinance, and (b) authorize deviations from the terms of the Town's Zoning Ordinances relating to setback and frontage requirements, height limitations, lot size restrictions, yard and building requirements, subdivision regulations, and other requirements unrelated to use, except for the buffer requirements established in the Ordinance.

segs.head: (7) Storage or stockpiling of materials is not permitted within 100 feet of a public right of way unless screened by a masonry wall or a wall composed of similar material.
segs.text: (7) Storage or stockpiling of materials is not permitted within 100 feet of a public right of way unless screened by a masonry wall or a wall composed of similar material. Florida DEP permitted Class I Landfills and accessory uses are not subject to this requirement. Storage or stockpiling of materials is only allowed in accordance with this requirement for uses approved by special exception or determined by the Town to be a lawful use existing at the time of passage of the Ordinance.

segs.head: (8) Requires a Development Agreement between the Town and Property Owner for Class I and Class III Landfills, but not for other types of Solid Waste Facilities.
segs.text: (8) Requires a Development Agreement between the Town and Property Owner for Class I and Class III Landfills, but not for other types of Solid Waste Facilities.

segs.head: (9) Provisions relating to existing uses of land and buildings, even if the use does not conform to the new Ordinance, have been included.
segs.text: (9) Provisions relating to existing uses of land and buildings, even if the use does not conform to the new Ordinance, have been included. An existing lawful use of a building may be continued: (a) as long as no structural changes are made, unless required by law or Ordinance, and (b) the use is not extended to occupy any land outside the existing building. An existing lawful use of land may be continued provided: (a) the use shall not be enlarged or increased; and (b) the use may not be extended to occupy a greater area of land than occupied by the use at the time of adoption of the Ordinance. A "Lawful Use" shall be evidenced by either: (a) Town Council approval of the use prior to adoption of the Ordinance; or (b) a Final Certificate of Use authorizing all components of the use issued prior to the adoption of the Ordinance. (10)Solid Waste Facilities and accessory uses authorized and existing pursuant to a Development Agreement that is valid and effective prior to the adoption of the Page 2 September 26, 2016 Ordinance on Solid Waste Facilities Ordinance are exempt from the provisions of the Ordinance. Modifications, alterations or expansions are subject to Town approval to be included in either a new Development Agreement or amendment to the existing Development Agreement. Staff Requests/Communications 14 -Adjournment Reading of Minutes: The minutes of prior Council Meetings shall not be read aloud but the Council shall consider corrections of minutes of the immediate prior meeting(s) upon request by any member of the Town Council. Unless a reading of the minutes is requested by a Council Member, minutes may be approved by motion as part of the Consent Agenda. Consent Agenda: There shall be a Consent Agenda during each Regular Council Meeting. The Consent Agenda shall contain Resolutions, approval of minutes, motions and other pertinent matters which, in the opinion of the Mayor and Staff may be handled and implemented without necessity for discussion. Unless a member of the Council specifically requests that an item be removed from the Consent Agenda for discussion, all items shall be approved and adopted by a single motion and roll call vote. Time for Presentations/Comments on an Agenda Item: Presentations will be limited to no more than ten (10) minutes and speakers for or against an Agenda item shall be limited to no more than three (3) minutes. Presenters have two (2) minutes to rebut each speaker against the item presented or to otherwise clarify points necessary to allow a decision by the Town Council. Order of Vote: Roll call shall be by order of seating. segs.text: (2) The method of compensation and its limitations are illustrated by the following examples: (i) If an employee is scheduled to begin his/her shift at 3:00 p.m., and appears in court for the period from 9:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. [four (4) hours], the employee will receive off-duty court time compensation for the actual four (4) hours spent on off-duty court time. (ii) If an employee is scheduled to begin his/her shift at 3:00 p.m., and appears in court for the period from 9:00 a.m. to 11:00 a.m. [two (2) hours], the employee will receive off-duty court time compensation for the three (3) hour minimum. (iii) If an employee is scheduled to begin PBA Proposals October 11, 2017 his/her shift at 3:00 p.m, and appears in court for the period from 10:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. [six (6) hours], the employee will receive off-duty court time compensation for five (5) hours. [The remaining one (1) hour of off- duty court time will be compensated at the employee's regular hourly rate of pay.] (iv) If an employee is scheduled to begin his/her shift at 3:00 p.m., and appears in court for the period of 1:00 - 1:30 p.m. [one-half (1/2) hour], the employee will receive off- duty court time compensation for two (2) hours (for the period from 1:00 p.m. to 3:00 p.m.). segs.head: (2) For purposes of this article, a "preventable crash" means a crash resulting from the employee's negligent or reckless operation of a Town vehicle, regardless of the extent of any property damage or physical injuries which result from the crash.
segs.text: (2) For purposes of this article, a "preventable crash" means a crash resulting from the employee's negligent or reckless operation of a Town vehicle, regardless of the extent of any property damage or physical injuries which result from the crash. When an employee assigned to drive a Town vehicle as part of his or her regular duties is not involved in a preventable crash, as determined by the Police Chief, during any consecutive twelve (12) month period after October 1, 2005, a "Safe Driving Award" of eight (8) hours of vacation time shall be added to his or her vacation bank for the year in which the twelfth (12th) month ends. For an employee who is involved in a preventable crash, as determined by the Police Chief, the employee's new twelve (12) month period shall begin on the next calendar day following the date of the preventable crash. A newly hired employee shall begin accumulating time for purposes of participating in this incentive on the first calendar day following the completion of his or her probati n.

segs.head: - Discussion and Action on the Request for Price Increase for the Home Care Senior Services Program.
votes: Councilperson Ayala made a motion as follows, TO ACCEPT AND APPROVE THE $ 2.00 PRICE INCREASE AS PROPOSED BY SENIOR CARE SERVICES, INC EFFECTIVE SEPTEMBER 1, 2021. Councilwoman Ayala seconded the motion, and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Request for Price Increase for the Home Care Senior Services Program. Social Services Director Lizmari Valido approached the Town Council and explained that although there was not a formal contract in effect with the vendor, the company providing the services had requested a $ 2.00 per hour price increase effective September 1, 2021, totaling to $ 16.00 per hour. Director Valido further explained that the current weekly cost for the services totals $ 266.00, and considering the proposed new rate, the weekly cost would total about $ 304.00 making the annual cost of the price increase $ 2,000. Senior Care Services, Inc representative Ana Ponce located at 6356 Manor Lane, Suite 103 South Miami Florida 33143 also approached the Town Council and informed the Town Council that a price increase had not been requested since 2015. Without further discussion, Councilperson Ayala made a motion as follows, TO ACCEPT AND APPROVE THE $ 2.00 PRICE INCREASE AS PROPOSED BY SENIOR CARE SERVICES, INC EFFECTIVE SEPTEMBER 1, 2021. Councilwoman Ayala seconded the motion, and it was carried unanimously.

segs.head: - Discussion and Action on the Request for Price Increase for the Town of Medley Hot Meal Program.
votes: Vice-Mayor Pacheco made a motion as follows, TO ACCEPT AND APPROVE THE $ 2.65 PRICE INCREASE AS PROPOSED BY LATIN AMERCAN GRILL, TOTALLING $ 7.70 PER MEAL EFFECTIVE IMMEDITELY. Councilperson Ayala seconded the motion, and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Request for Price Increase for the Town of Medley Hot Meal Program. Rainier Gonzalez, owner of R.G.H Corporation D/B/A Latin American Grill located at 12638 Pines Boulevard Pembroke Pines, Florida 33027 approached the Town Council to formally request an approval of the proposed price increase of $ 2.65 per meal for the services provided under the Hot Meal Program. Mr. Gonzalez further stated that new total price would be $7.70 per meal effective immediately in addition to a mutual understanding that both parties can come back and renegotiate the price of the services at any time if the economy environment changes. Without further discussion, Vice-Mayor Pacheco made a motion as follows, TO ACCEPT AND APPROVE THE $ 2.65 PRICE INCREASE AS PROPOSED BY LATIN AMERCAN GRILL, TOTALLING $ 7.70 PER MEAL EFFECTIVE IMMEDITELY. Councilperson Ayala seconded the motion, and it was carried unanimously. It was noted for the record that Town Attorney Lillian Arango joined the meeting during the discussion of the item.

segs.head: - Discussion and Action on the Salary Study and Gender Analysis for the Town of Medley Prepared by Evergreen Solutions, LLC.

segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Salary Study and Gender Analysis for the Town of Medley Prepared by Evergreen Solutions, LLC. Special Labor Counsel Lyndsey Rider approached the Council and gave a brief introduction of the services performed by Nancy Berkley with Evergreen Solutions, LLC located at 2878 Remington Green Circle Tallahassee, Florida 32308. It was also stated that services provided by Evergreen Solutions, LLC had been requested and approved by Council to conduct a salary survey and gender analysis in response to anonymous complaints of pay inequality between male and female department directors received in 2020. Nancy Berkley addressed the Town Council and discussed a power point presentation that included a report of the study process, positions reviewed, current conditions, classification review, equity review, compensation review, identified proposed pay ranges and slotting and salary adjustment implementation. Ms. Berkely further explained that the process included collection of the data the Town provided which included position descriptions and employee data files along with Town s pay practices. In addition, it was also explained that clear definitions of the job duties and minimum qualifications specifically were asked from the Town since they were not immediately identified when data was received the first time. segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Request for Job Availability for One (1) Administrative Position for the Capital Improvements and Economic Development Department. Human Resources Director Olga Quin addressed the Town Council to request clarification on the matter since it was not clear whether the Council, during the last discussion during the July 15 budget meeting about the request, wished to move forward with filling the position. The Council then, in a consensus fashion, clarified that the part-time administrative assistant position was to move forward and be noticed and filled. However, the full-time position previously requested and approved is to be on hold until the next fiscal year 2021-2022. Without further discussion, Mayor Martell made a motion as follows, TO PROCEED WITH THE NOTICE OF JOB AVAILABILITY OF THE PART- TIME ADMINISTRATIVE POSITION AND HOLD THE FULL-TIME POSITION PREVIOSULY REQUESTED AND APPROVED UNTIL FISCAL YEAR 2021-2022. segs.head: - Discussion and Action on the Appointment of an Interim and Successor Building Official for the Town of Medley Building and Zoning Department.
segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Appointment of an Interim and Successor Building Official for the Town of Medley Building and Zoning Department. Building and Zoning Director Richard McConachie approached the Council and informed them that as previously informed, he will be retiring effective December 31, 2021. Therefore, and taking into consideration the qualifications and experience he recommended William Guillermo Diaz to undertake the duties and responsibilities of the Director of Building and Zoning/Building Official. Director McConachie further stated that Mr. Diaz has helped oversee the Town s permitting and violation process as well as has worked with the staff to improve all aspects of the department for the past 8 years. In addition, director McConachie stated that it was proposed for Mr. Diaz to begin in an interim status effective October 1, 2021 and in full capacity effective January 1, 2022 having full authority of the operations in his absence. Director McConachie thanked the Town and all the staff for all the years shared. Vice-Mayor Pacheco then asked about the base salary that would be assigned to Mr. Diaz considering the Town s recently provided compensation study information to which the Mayor responded that the salary had already been discussed and agreed upon. Therefore, it was stated the annual salary would be $125,000 a year which was the starting salary previously assigned to the prior Building and Zoning/Building Official. segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Interior Improvements of the Multiuse Training Room & Kitchen Renovations of Medley Municipal Services Facility (MMSF). Capital Improvement and Economic Development director Jorge Corzo approached the podium to address the item and explained that bids were received for the project, and they were higher than expected he would like to re-bid the project including a more direct solicitation process. Mr. Corzo further stated that although the project was initiated as an internal upgrade/repair project he was asked to help since there was an insurance claim involved. In addition, Mr. Corzo explained the historical need on which the project was initiated which included a most robust kitchen to support the Town s Emergency Operations. However, because the needs of the Town for a more robust kitchen, compliance with certain construction codes would be required that included stainless steel appliances, the need for a grease trap amongst others elevating the cost of the project in the process. Mr. Corzo also stated that the increase of building supplies has not helped the overall cost of the bids received for the project. Town Clerk Victoria Martinez reminded the Town Engineer that the space and room in question serves as the designated area for the Miami-Dade County Elections Department and the Town s department elections process. segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Request to Waive Early Retirement Penalty for the Town of Medley General Pension Plan. Finance Director Roy Danziger addressed the item and stated that the Town has in the past applied the same benefit to the police pension plan and has allowed employees to retire early. Thus, he would like to also extend the same to employees who have at least 24 years of full-time service. Mayor Roberto Martell then stated that a 90-day window has been extended to the police department and so he would like to do the same, to be consistent, to participants of the Town s pension plan. Director Danziger then informed the Town Council that if proposal is approved, there would be 2 potential qualifying participants of the general pension plan. Town s special labor counsel Lindsey Ryder joined the discussion and stated that if the Council approved said benefit, it would have to be presented to the FPE barraging unit for consideration and approval since one of the 2 qualifying individuals is a member of the bargaining unit. In addition, special labor Counsel Ryder confirmed that 90-day window is what has been presented to the other bargaining unit in the past. Finance Director Roy Danziger further stated that if approved, the October regular meeting would be the target day to bring back a resolution to formalize the action. Without further discussion, Councilwoman Stefano made a motion as follows, TO OPEN AN EARLY 90 DAY RETIREMENT WINDOW AND WAIVE THE EARLY RETITREM

segs.head: - Discussion and Action on Town of Medley Events.
votes: Councilwoman Stefano made a motion as follows, TO ALLOW TIME FLEXIBILITY TO THE ARTS AND CARFTS EVENTS IN ACCORDANCE WITH ITS OPERATIONS AS LONG AS AGREED UPON BY COUNCIL. Councilperson Ayala seconded the motion, and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: - Discussion and Action on Town of Medley Events. Councilwoman Stefano addressed the matter and stated that the purpose of the item is to provide staff with flexibility to change the time of certain events. Social Services and Parks and Recreations Director Lizmari Valido inquired whether the flexibility of the event s timing was to coordinate for any of the Councilmembers to perform the transportation to the event in question. Councilwoman Stefano confirmed director Valido s question and further stated that in the case of the Arts & Crafts event, the change the timing of the event only would be used to coordinate the transportation of said event being performed by the Council. Director Valido further stated that if in the case of a change, the rest of the Town Council would be consulted to make sure the new time would be agreed upon. Vice-Mayor Pacheco stated whether the need to meet monthly to discuss Town events was necessary. Councilwoman Stefano then stated that perhaps every month was not necessary but at least quarterly meetings were appropriate to discuss Town events since there are several events that require planning in advance like the Thanksgiving, Halloween, and Christmas events and since the councilmembers are also allowed to do events on their own. The Council agreed in a consensus manner that quarterly events would best fit the Council after the workshop scheduled for September 7, 2021 takes place. segs.head: - Discussion and Action on the Appointment of one (1) Licensing Permit Clerk II for the Building and Zoning Department.
votes: Mayor Martell then placed a motion as follows, "TO APPOINT SCARLETT URREGO-MOLINA TO THE POSITION OF LICENSING PERMIT CLERK II, EFFECTIVE DECEMBER 7, 2021." Councilwoman Ayala seconded the motion and it carried unanimously.
segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Appointment of one (1) Licensing Permit Clerk II for the Building and Zoning Department. Building and Zoning Director Richard McConachie and Interim Building Official William Diaz approached the council to recommend the appointment of Scarlett Urrego-Molina to the position of Building Licensing Clerk II. He continued to state that she is an exceptionally employee that has proven herself to be a great asset to the building department. Mayor Martell then placed a motion as follows, "TO APPOINT SCARLETT URREGO-MOLINA TO THE POSITION OF LICENSING PERMIT CLERK II, EFFECTIVE DECEMBER 7, 2021." Councilwoman Ayala seconded the motion and it carried unanimously. Mr. McConachie took a moment to express, in lieu of his retirement announcement,how he has enjoyed working for the Town of Medley and has appreciated being apart of the family. He expressed how the Town has exceptional employees to work with, and how he feels proud of how his efforts has allowed for the growth of commerce of the Town and helped the residents. Mr. McConachie also mentioned appreciation for Human Resources Director Olga Quin for her help and improvements to the Building Department.

segs.head: - Discussion and Action on the Renewal of the Town of Medley Medical Insurance Policy.
segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Renewal of the Town of Medley Medical Insurance Policy. Bob Reynolds from Morris and Reynolds, the Town's insurance agent and representative, began his discussion by addressing the medical insurance policies and explaining that he has negotiated five different offers with leading companies that first resulted in Cigna offering an initial zero percent increase,then a 2%reduced rate offer, and ultimately,after continued negotiations,a 15%reduction was received. Mr. Reynolds continued and stated that in 2022, the premium funded by the Town is expected to see savings of$253,0000 which will be noted as the biggest reduction ever received by the Town. Also,employees paying for dependent coverage will see a reduction in price as well. Without further discussion,Mayor Martell placed a motion as follows, "TO APPROVE CIGNA'S PROPOSAL AND RENEW THE TOWN OF MEDLEY MEDICAL INSURANCE POLICY WITH CIGNA FOR THE 2022 YEAR EFFECTIVE JANUARY 1, 2022."

segs.head: - Discussion and Action on the Town of Medley Medical Transportation Program.
segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Town of Medley Medical Transportation Program. Director Valido addressed the documentation provided in the agenda packages and mentioned some corrections made to the job description presented for Social Services and Parks and Recreation CDL Driver position. The changes, as stated by director Valido, included driver s license endorsement language and the non-exempt status applicable to the position. Director Valido also mentioned that the need for a social services driver has existed for a while now and because former employee Osvaldo has now retired, and the new school year is scheduled to begin August 23 the need is overgrowing. Thus, director Valido continued to address the options presented for the operations of the social services medical transportation program which included part-time and full-time position options in conjunction with the arts and crafts, CITT shopping route and music night events schedule. Director Valido and the Town Council discussed of options 1, 3 and 4 in detail, explaining how the Uber Health program is structured and how it is proposed to work with the Town s medical transportation program, along with the pros and cons of both, a full-time and part- time position were had. In addition, director Valido discussed the participation of the medical transportation program for the last three (3) months and analyzed the participation it in detail with the recommended options. After a brief discussion, Councilperson Stefano

segs.head: - Discussion and Action on the Request for Job Availability of One (1) or More Social Services and Parks and Recreation CDL Driver Position.

segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Request for Job Availability of One (1) or More Social Services and Parks and Recreation CDL Driver Position. Having discussed the options proposed for the social services medical transportation program, it was decided to approve and make available a part-time social services and parks and recreation CD driver position. Without further discussion, Councilwoman Stefano made a motion as follows, TO APPROVE THE REQUEST FOR ONE (1) PART-TIME PARKS AND RECREATION SOCIAL SERVICES CDL DRIVER POSITION FOR THE SOCIAL SERVICES AND PARKS AND RECREATIONS DEPARTMENT. Vice-Mayor Pacheco seconded the motion, and it was carried unanimously. Councilperson Ayala also took a moment to recognize Lieutenant Arturo Jinete for his 30 years of service to the Town. Councilperson Ayala also asked Town staff to prepare a small gathering to celebrate such a tenure that perhaps could take place after the next scheduled council meeting and to also include utilities director Jorge Soto who had recently reached 35 years of service. segs.head: - Special Presentation by Vice-Mayor Pacheco to Dade County Mayor Daniella Levine Cava and the Florida Department of Health in Miami-Dade County for the Outstanding COVID-19 Vaccine Outreach Events in the Town of Medley.
votes: Mayor Martell then moved to place a motion as follows, "TO APPOINT KORY JOHNSON AND IVAN PAZ AS FULL TIME POLICE OFFICERS FOR THE TOWN OF MEDLEY POLICE DEPARTMENT Councilperson Stefano seconded and it carried unanimously.

Mayor Martell then placed a motion as follows, "TO APPOINT ANTONELLA MORA, AND JULIAN BERNAL AS PART-TIME COMMUNITY SERVICE AIDS FOR THE TOWN OF MEDLEY POLICE DEPARTMENT" Councilwoman Ayala seconded the motion and it carried unanimously.
segs.text: - Special Presentation by Vice-Mayor Pacheco to Dade County Mayor Daniella Levine Cava and the Florida Department of Health in Miami-Dade County for the Outstanding COVID-19 Vaccine Outreach Events in the Town of Medley. Miami Dade County Mayor Daniella Cava approached the podium and thanked the Mayor and Vice Mayor for their invitation. She then continued to explain how she is taking the time to visit all the cities in the county to help build a relationship of partnership between the County and the cities. Mayor Cava explained how she fought hard by spearheading efforts in getting availability of the COVID-19 vaccine out into the communities. Mayor Martell then, on behalf of the Medley Council, congratulated Mayor Cava on her initiatives and then presented her with a key of the city. Vice Mayor also thanked Mayor Cava and recognized her and her team for their response time when vaccines were scarce, but most needed in the community, and he also thanked Commissioner Jose Pepe Diaz for his behind-the-scenes efforts in assisting in acquiring vaccines for the Town of Medley. Vice-Mayor Pacheco then presented Ms. Cava with a recognition from the citizens, the Medley Town Council, and the Medley Police Department. Vice Mayor Pacheco continued to also express the Town s gratitude to the Florida Department of Health in Miami Dade County for the outstanding COVID-19 vaccine outreach events held in the Town. The following Health department personnel were recognized for their efforts:

votes: Councilwoman Ayala placed a motion as follows, "TO AUTHORIZE THE MAYOR AND TOWN ATTORNEY TO ENTER INTO ANY NECCESARY AGREEMENT FOR THE USE OF TOWN S FACILITIES WITH THE FLORIDA INTERNATIONAL UNIVERSITY (FIU) FOR THE COVID-19 BAUM RESEARCH COMMUNITY OUTREACH PROJECT" Councilwoman Stefano seconded and it carried unanimously.
segs.text: - Request by the Social Services and Parks and Recreations Department for Discussion and Action on the COVID-19 Baum Research Community Outreach Project Conducted by Florida International University (FIU). David Brown, from the Florida International University (FIU) college of medicine, requested to utilize Town facilities to conduct a study based on COVID-19 responses. The proposal as presented is based on studies that would involve COVID-19 testing to document community responses to the COVID-19 pandemic, as well as conducting surveys, responses on exposure to COVID-19 and community sentiment on vaccinations. The study would also include June 7, 2021 Regular Council Meeting Minutes COVID-19 testing, and bloodwork on site. Without further discussion, Councilwoman Ayala placed a motion as follows, "TO AUTHORIZE THE MAYOR AND TOWN ATTORNEY TO ENTER INTO ANY NECCESARY AGREEMENT FOR THE USE OF TOWN S FACILITIES WITH THE FLORIDA INTERNATIONAL UNIVERSITY (FIU) FOR THE COVID-19 BAUM RESEARCH COMMUNITY OUTREACH PROJECT" Councilwoman Stefano seconded and it carried unanimously.

segs.head: - Discussion and Action on the Town of Medley Social Services Program s Rules and Regulations.
segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Town of Medley Social Services Program s Rules and Regulations. Social Services and Parks and Recreation Director Lizmari Valido approached the Council and addressed the documentation provided for said item that included proposed changes as previously discussed during the May 6, 2021 Council workshop. Proposed changes as provided addressed existing rules and regulations to programs administered by the Social Services department. In addition, director Valido specifically addressed the Start-Up Grant program and recommended not to penalize students for the circumstances and outcomes because of the global pandemic of 2020. Director Valido continued to recommend not to take grades into consideration for the 2020 school year so that a Start-Up applicant would not be affected. Councilwoman Ayala expressed agreement with the recommendations. Councilwoman Stefano then addressed the Hot Meal program and inquired about a particular case of a resident that applied for the meal program and issues were found. Hot Meal program director Fatima Fuentes approached the podium and began to explain that an application was received from an individual who has a physical debilitation. However, the rules and regulations in existence do not address nor allows for exceptions to be made. Director Fuentes then asked that if the Council wished to consider said circumstances, the authorization to take applicants on a case-by-case basis was then required. Without further disc

segs.head: - Discussion, Action and Ratification on the Appointment of the Assistant to the Council Position.
segs.text: - Discussion, Action and Ratification on the Appointment of the Assistant to the Council Position. Town Attorney Lilian Arango addressed the matter by stating that the job description had been presented for Council review and approval as instructed in the Council workshop of May 25, 2021. Ms. Arango reiterated that after further research it was determined that the position was clerical in nature and did not meet the exempt status. Vice Mayor Pacheco stated that he was not in agreement with the position s compensation matching the Councilmember s salary and he suggested for the council to wait on the pending gender study to determine the proper salary for this position. Human Resources Director Olga addressed the Council and clarified that she had previously misspoken regarding the current wage that Rosa Palau was making. Director Quin also urged the Council to set a starting wage rate at this time with the tentative effective date of June 15 while also taking into consideration the current wage rate of individuals currently fulfilling the same position having higher education, qualifications, tenure and experience. Councilperson Ayala stated that he believed a starting wage of $24.00 was reasonable. After a brief discussion it was determined to set a starting wage to $23.00 dollars an hour. Town Clerk Victoria Martinez stated that as the documentation provided stated, the following conditions will apply to the position.

segs.head: - Item 13(A)11 Request by Councilperson Ayala for Discussion and Action on the Town Events Allocated Funds Program.
segs.text: - Item 13(A)11 Request by Councilperson Ayala for Discussion and Action on the Town Events Allocated Funds Program. Councilperson Ayala began the discussion by requesting to reduce the funds from $1,000.00 a month as previously approved to $7,000 a year per Councilperson per fiscal year. Town Attorney Arango explained that public funds need to be spent on public means for the community. In addition, attorney Arango further explained that spending on individuals can be problematic, thus expenditures shall generally be made to provide a public benefit. Vice Mayor Pacheco disagreed with the proposal, and it was noted that he did not want to participation in the allocation of said funds. June 7, 2021 Regular Council Meeting Minutes Without further discussion on the matter, Councilperson Ayala then placed a motion as follows, "TO ALLOCATE $7000.00 FOR EACH COUNCILPERSON FOR THE EXCEPTION OF VICE-MAYOR PACHECO TO BE USED WITHIN THE FISCAL YEAR FOR TOWN OF MEDLEY EVENTS. FUNDS TO BE SUBJECT TO LEGAL GUILDELINES TO BE PROVIDED BY THE TOWN ATTONEY." Councilwoman Ayala seconded and the votes were cast as follows, Vice-Mayor Ivan Pacheco- No Councilwoman Lily Stefano- Yes Councilperson Edgar Ayala- Yes Councilwoman Lizelh Ayala- Yes Mayor Roberto Martell- No The motion passed by majority of vote. segs.head: - Update by Town Clerk on the Translation Services and Audio-Visual Improvements Previously Requested for Public Meetings.
segs.text: - Update by Town Clerk on the Translation Services and Audio-Visual Improvements Previously Requested for Public Meetings. Ms. Martinez updated the Council on the current research and reviewed the documentation presented to the as the result of the services and upgrades requested by the Council. Town Clerk Martinez also stated that equipment presented is used by neighboring cities and accommodates what is considered the hybrid meeting platform and possibly the abilities to provide translation services for the meetings through the closed caption capabilities of said equipment and services. It was also noted that the Clerk s office is pending an estimate from said company and it will be presented to the Council once it is received for further review, comments discussion and/or approval. Town Clerk Martinez also stated that said improvements may be eligible to receive some state and/or federal fund as funding was approved for local governments to make improvements of this nature as they were necessary during the pandemic. This will be further researched.

segs.head: - Monthly Update by Town Staff on Current Town Projects and Related Finances.
segs.text: - Monthly Update by Town Staff on Current Town Projects and Related Finances. Finance Director Roy Danziger approached the Council and distributed a 2021 assessment from the Property Appraisers and explained that the Town experienced a 6.7% increase from last year s initial assessment of $2,648,409,814.00, and although the Town does not have the final assessment, this is a positive review. Finance Director Roy Danziger circulated a second piece of documentation which reflected the amount of funds distributed to cities under the CARES Act and suggested using the funds for water infrastructure improvements. It was also discussed and announced that the office of the Town clerk is working with the finance department to schedule budget workshops and necessary public meetings for the Town s budget for the June 7, 2021 Regular Council Meeting Minutes 2021-2022 fiscal year. Assistant Utilities Director Osmanny Larzabal approached the Council and stated that the Town experienced an unusually high bill for Stormwater in the month of May. Mr. Larzabal further stated that the Town s assumptions are that the issue may be an error with Miami Dade County s readings to which Director Soto is already inquiring and addressing as such. Director Jorge Corzo also approached the Council and gave a brief update on some ongoing projects. segs.head: - Further Discussion on the Proposed Services Agreement with River North Transit,LLC For On-Demand Commuter Transit Circulator Services in the Town of Medley.
segs.text: - Further Discussion on the Proposed Services Agreement with River North Transit,LLC For On-Demand Commuter Transit Circulator Services in the Town of Medley. Jorge Corzo, Director of the Capital Improvements and Economic Development department gave an overview of the items presented for discussion. In continuance, Stuart Robinson from Kimley- Horn&Associates carried out a presentation about the Multimodal Transportation plan adopted by the Town in 2017 which addressed bicycle and transportation methods that included circulators. It was stated that the Town had received a grant from the Florida Department of Transportation (FDOT) for the eastern corridor to the community that included a 30-minute loop running transportation route. Thus, said services could be advantageous for the NW 79 Place,North of NW 74 street and East of the intersection of NW 74 Avenue and West 12 Street. In continuance Olivia Blahut from River North Transit,LLC went over a presentation(see attached) that included a video of current transportation services provided in the city of Arlington Texas that included case studies, benefits to riders and communities as well as the necessary steps to follow. The presentation included the explanation of Micro Transit services that are currently in service in Miami-Dade County, Broward County, Fort-Lauderdale, City of Gainesville, Orlando and many more along with the overview of Go Connect transportation services that are also in existence in Miami-Dade County. segs.head: - Discussion on the Unsolicited Proposal by Warehouse Renting, LLC for Lease of Town Owned Land Located at 10791 NW South River Drive(Folio No. 22-2033- 001-0771).
segs.text: - Discussion on the Unsolicited Proposal by Warehouse Renting, LLC for Lease of Town Owned Land Located at 10791 NW South River Drive(Folio No. 22-2033- 001-0771). Director Corzo addressed the item and stated that the request for the lease do not fall under the unsolicited proposal guidelines set and adopted by the Town and it would be a policy decision whether the Town chooses to lease the land in question. Town legal representative Pete Waldman of Weiss Serota and Helfman addressed the Town Council and explained that the Town has already survey the property and the value was estimated by Slack, Johnston and Magenheimer, Inc. who has experience with Medley's property history. In addition, attorney Waldman recommended the Town to enter into a license agreement which would protect the Town and would give flexibility with the Right-Of-Way program for future projects and license agreements. Attorney Waldman further stated that, if need, the license agreement could be revoked with 180 days' notice should the Town wish rather than entering a lease that could require the Town to pay should the Town decide to terminate the long-term lease. After a brief discussion, it was decided that an appraisal be performed for the Town property in question and for the matter to come back to council for further discussion and/or approval.

segs.head: - Discussion and Action on the Renewal of the Town of Medley Business Insurance Policy.
votes: councilperson Ayala placed a motion as follows, TO RENEW THE TOWN OF MEDLEY BUSINESS INSURANCE POLICY AS RECOMMENDED EFFECTIVE 11/01/2021. Mayor Martell seconded, and it carried unanimously.
segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Renewal of the Town of Medley Business Insurance Policy. Bob Reynolds from Morris and Reynolds Insurance addressed the Mayor and Council and began to discuss his recommendation for the renewal of the Town s business insurance policy. He also gave an update on the Town s medical insurance upcoming policy renewal and announced that there will be zero increase in the Cigna healthcare plan for 2022. However, Mr. Reynolds also stated that competitive rates from other insurance companies had been received and hopes to negotiate a reduction for the Town. Mr. Reynolds further informed the Town of the increase in the cyber security liability portion of the policy driven by claim severity and frequency of the market for this matter. Thus, it was recommended to renew with Axis as they continue to be the most competitive in terms of pricing and broad coverage. It was also instructed that all department heads review the list of vehicles under the Town s general auto and insurance liability policy and advise if any are not in use so they may be sold and removed from the policy. Without further discussion councilperson Ayala placed a motion as follows, TO RENEW THE TOWN OF MEDLEY BUSINESS INSURANCE POLICY AS RECOMMENDED EFFECTIVE 11/01/2021. Mayor Martell seconded, and it carried unanimously.

segs.text: - Discussion and Action on New Proposed Commercial Water and Sewer Rates and Results of the Water and Sewer Study Performed by Tetra Tech. Finance Director Roy Danziger began addressing the matter by discussing the handout included in the agenda package which was previously circulated for the council and went over his recommendations from the water and sewer rates study as highlighted. Director Danziger further stated that the recommendation for the water is to raise the rate to $9.34 for every 1000 gallons over the 5000 gallons consumption with a base rate of $53.80, and the sewer recommendation is to raise the rate to $6.76 per every 1000 over the 5000 gallons consumption. Director Danziger also stated that the average bill increase will be 9% and that the water rates would basically remain as and reflecting said change in the base rate according to meter size. It was also stated that changes as proposed would generate an estimated revenue of $300,000 a year but the increase would not be burden on the minimal and average users but on the heavier consumers. Finance Director Danziger continued and stated that the recommendation is to have the increase effective by the January billing thus bringing it before council in the December regular meeting for final review and approval. Utilities Director Jorge Soto joined the discussion and explained that luckily the infiltration of rain has been recently low but there are many necessary and ongoing repairs to the sewer system. Councilwoman Ayala briefly defined gentrification as the process whereby the character of a poor urban area is changed by wealthier people moving in, improving housing, and attracting new businesses, typically displacing current inhabitants in the process. In addition, she explained that the current resident s average income is thirty thousand a year and they would not benefit from this project. Director Corzo stated that the plan has zero effect on gentrification because there are no residential components in the plan as the proposal goes hand and hand with economic growth and employment opportunities. segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Appeal of the Administrative Review Board Regarding Ms. Olga Quin. The Mayor then began the discussion by stating his intent to affirm the employment termination of Ms. Olga Quin and to reverse the administrative review board's recommendation. Councilperson Ayala then asked for clarification on the Administrative Review Boards decision. Therefore, Town Attorney Michael Pizzi presented the transcript which stated that the Administrative Review Board Hearing findings resulted in a 2/1 vote from the appointee members, whereas the majority recommended for the Town to reverse their termination of Ms. Olga Quin. Mr. Pizzi continued to state that the Mayor's intent is to appeal that recommendation and to affirm the termination of said employee. It was also noted that the Mayor was to abstain unless the vote is tied. Councilwoman Ayala read into the record the following statement from the transcript as follows, "The finding determined that the due process had been violated in terms of timing and hearing, and that the termination was not justified by record." Councilwoman Ayala also stated her agreement with the Administrative Review Board's decision. Without further discussion, Vice-Mayor Pacheco then placed a motion as follows, "TO AFFIRM THE EMPLOYMENT TERMINATION OF MS.OLGA QUIN AND TO REVERSE THE ADMINISTRATIVE REVIEW BOARD'S RECOMMENDATION." Councilwoman Pacheco seconded the motion, and the votes were cast as follows, Vice-Mayor Ivan Pacheco- Yes C

segs.head: - Resolution C-2053 Approving Work Order and Proposal with Snubbs Consulting Inc. to Provide Professional Engineering Services for 2023 Consent Decree Compliance Continuing Services.
votes: Mayor Martell then placed a motion to adopt Resolution C-2053 as presented. Councilwoman Pacheco seconded the motion, and the resolution was adopted unanimously.
segs.text: - Resolution C-2053 Approving Work Order and Proposal with Snubbs Consulting Inc. to Provide Professional Engineering Services for 2023 Consent Decree Compliance Continuing Services. Town Attorney Michael Pizzi explained that the County is under a consent decree where the state and federal government require them to clean up the sewer system and take steps to fix the sewer system | back up. Mr. Pizzi further explained that the Town of Medley, as part of Miami-Dade County and part of that system, is required to also comply with the consent decree and Snubbs Consulting currently has an agreement with the Water and Sewer Department. Thus, the item presented is a work order under that agreement for Snubbs Consulting to continue to inspect the sewer system and report their findings to the County so the Town is in compliance with the consent agreement. Vice-Mayor Ayala expressed concerns with using the same consultants without carrying out continued RFP process. Town Attorney Pizzi agreed that a periodic RFQ s can be performed to comply with the Town s Procurement Ordinance. Mayor Martell then placed a motion to adopt Resolution C-2053 as presented. Councilwoman Pacheco seconded the motion, and the resolution was adopted unanimously.

segs.head: - Discussion and Action on the Town of Medley 2020 Annexation Application with Miami- Dade County.
segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Town of Medley 2020 Annexation Application with Miami- Dade County. Town Attorney Pizzi explained that the County Mayor had vetoed the annexation applications presented by the Town of Medley and the Town of Virginia Gardens due to the contention of the mitigation payments. Attorney Pizzi further stated that the items were rescheduled for consideration before the board of commissioners for January 2023 and explained that the Miami-Dade County board of commissioners include 6 new commissioners who may not be familiar with the Town of Medley annexation application history. Thus, the application would be in front of the commissioners for reconsideration requiring a total of 9 votes for passage, otherwise the Town could face a redo of the annexation application process and start all over again. Attorney Pizzi explained the current options given the circumstances which include the following,

segs.head: - Ifthe vetoed decision is overridden by the Board of commissioners, The Town of Medley application moves forward with no issues to be concerned.
segs.text: - Ifthe vetoed decision is overridden by the Board of commissioners, The Town of Medley application moves forward with no issues to be concerned.

segs.head: - Ifthe vetoed decision is not overridden, the Town of Medley annexation application goes back to square one and the Town would have to decide on whether move forward with the annexation and a new Ordinance to presented accepting mitigation payments and have that considered and potentially passed on two readings with an interlocal agreement.
segs.text: - Ifthe vetoed decision is not overridden, the Town of Medley annexation application goes back to square one and the Town would have to decide on whether move forward with the annexation and a new Ordinance to presented accepting mitigation payments and have that considered and potentially passed on two readings with an interlocal agreement. Process could take a few months and current proposed mitigation payments $517000 a year for 7 years.

segs.text: - Consideration of Senator s Garcia motion to reconsider the item which supersedes the vote on the vetoed decision and includes the option to have the commissioners re-vote on the November 15, 2022 Town of Medley approval. However, Mr. Pizzi further stated that if the motion to reconsider presented by Senator Garcia is heard and acted upon before the vetoed decision is discussed, the Town can between now and then negotiate and work on proposed language including amounts and methodology. In addition, the Town can argue that because the number one cause is police assistance, the county is saving millions of dollars and the fact that the Town is already providing police service to the areas in question. Attorney Pizzi also stated that it is possible that between now and then, the County hold their position as it is possible that changes happen regarding the mitigation payment amounts, time and calculations. segs.head: - Discussion on the Town of Medley Fee Schedule.
segs.text: - Discussion on the Town of Medley Fee Schedule. Town Clerk Victoria Martinez explained that the last Town of Medley fee schedule was adopted in 2015 which included a comprehensive scheduled that included all services and charges provided by the Town and its departments, including but not limited to the Social Services and Parks and Recreations, the Building and Zoning Department and Office of the Town Clerk. However, there was a need to update and expand the schedule to include fees for new services and processes. Building and Zoning director William Diaz approached the Town Council and explained the updates included in the proposed fee schedule for building and zoning services including explanations of new fees incorporated such as the technology fee and new permit fees. The implementation date was also discussed as well as notice requirements. Town Clerk Victoria Martinez explained that language was also added in some areas to reflect updated fees of the proposed fee schedule such as liens and information requests,that are currently charged at a set fee while the new proposed schedule includes the fees to be the actual cost of production of the records requested. Town Clerk Martinez continued to explain that the proposed fee schedule mirrors the Town of Medley Records Request Policy for consistency and general compliance with the Florida Records Law. Since there was no other matter to be discussed,the workshop adjourned at 2:32 pm. Victoria artinez, , CMC, Town Clerk TOWN

votes: Mayor Martell placed a motion to approve resolution C-1981. Councilwoman Pacheco seconded the motion, and the votes were cast as follow, Vice-Mayor Ivan Pacheco- Yes Councilmember Edgar Ayala- No Councilmember Lizelh Ayala- No Councilmember Karina Pacheco - Yes Mayor Roberto Martell- Yes The motion passed by majority of vote.
segs.text: - Resolution Rescinding Resolution C-1885, which Adopted a Town of Medley Policy Establishing a Process for the Recruitment and Hiring of Town Employees. Mayor Martell began the discussion by explaining that the purpose to rescind Resolution C-1885 is to revert the process to how it was prior to the adoption of the hiring policy. The prior practice involved Directors expressing to the Mayor their need to hire employees for their department. Thus, if the Mayor approves the request, then directors may move along and conduct the hiring process. Once the hiring process is concluded, directors would then present their recommendation for hire before the Mayor and Council for formal approval. Councilperson Ayala stated that the policy was created after concerns from the Vice Mayor for not being a part of the hiring process and the Town wanting to establish an efficient policy when hiring employees. He continued to address the directors present and requested that any director who may want to speak on the matter approach the podium. Director Corzo stood and explained that the hiring process for his department was excessively long and strenuous. Vice Mayor interjected to explain that he was pursuing transparency in the process but did not agree with making the directors feel uncomfortable in their choice of hire or to instruct them whom to choose for their department. It was noted that the process is longer for the police department, but not strenuous. Without further discussion, Mayor

segs.head: - All Town of Medley event flyers will read Town of Medley Mayor Roberto Martell and Town Council unless it is sponsored by a single councilmember.
segs.text: - All Town of Medley event flyers will read Town of Medley Mayor Roberto Martell and Town Council unless it is sponsored by a single councilmember. All flyers including Council and departmental flyers are to be approved by the Mayor and created by the social services and park and recreations department. It was reiterated that any events paid by the Town will read as the Mayor proposes. Vice Mayor Pacheco suggested adding each councilmember s name to the flyers and the Mayor was in agreement. Mayor Martell then placed a motion as follows, ALL TOWN COUNCIL EVENTS AND FIELDTRIPS TO BE APPROVED BY THE MAYOR AND SCHEDULED BY THE MAYOR S OFFICE IN ADDITION TO ALL EVENT WORKSHOPS THAT WILL ALSO NEED TO BE SCHEDULED BY THE MAYOR S OFFICE. segs.head: - Request by Mayor Martell for Discussion and Action on Lakeside Parcel B Project.
segs.text: - Request by Mayor Martell for Discussion and Action on Lakeside Parcel B Project. Mayor Martell proposed to revert to his initial intention for the property which was to allow the construction of a short term, long term, and extended care facility for the elderly residents. He then instructed Town Clerk Victoria Martinez to translate the discussion into the Spanish language for the audience present. Councilperson Ayala wanted clarification on how the mayor expects to accomplish this goal. The Mayor explained that a Request for Information is to be put out to the public to solicit an investor for the leasing of the property and construction of a senior care facility. The proposal would be to acquire a business that would provide short-term care, long term care, extended care, and medical care facility including a medical clinic and the Town would decide the best company and the terms. Councilperson Ayala reiterated that he would like to know how the Mayor plans to guarantee the qualification of every resident that seeks these services. Mr. Lowell Dunn, owner of the property in which Lakeside Retirement Park is located, approached the Council and agreed with the proposal of a senior services facility but suggested processing in a master plan format. In addition, Mr. Dunn stated that he would like to be informed on the ongoing process and offered his assistance in the matter. segs.text: - Request by Mayor Martell for Discussion and Action on Council Fund Allocation. Mayor Martell addressed the item and proposed for the Council to return the credit cards assigned through the previously approved allocated funds, effective immediately. Councilperson Ayala stated that he was never in agreement with being given public funds for Council use and has never used nor charged the card since it was given. Councilwoman Ayala also wanted to note that an annual stipend of seven thousand dollars ($ 7,000) had been previously approved and in that time, she has used two thousand three hundred dollars ($2,300) to promote science, technology, engineering, and mathematic programs (STEM), for the children of the after-school program. In continuance, Councilwoman Ayala reiterated that she used the funds as they were meant to be utilized. Vice Mayor Pacheco also stated that he did not need a credit card with public funds. Councilperson Ayala stated that although the intent of the funds was to allow for all members of the Council to have the opportunity to sponsor events for the residents, the intent now is for the Council to work together for the sake of Town and residents. Councilwoman Ayala then explained that a financial report should be properly documented and submitted, and that the lack there of, has led to the Town receiving repeated audit findings that are unethical. votes: Mayor Martell then placed a motion as follows, TO REMOVE ALL PREVIOUS TOWN ISSUED CREDIT CARDS FROM ALL DEPARTMENT HEADS WITH THE EXCEPTION OF THE MAYOR, THE CHIEF OF POLICE, THE TOWN ENGINEER, AND THE TOWN CLERK Councilperson Ayala seconded the motion, and it carried unanimously.
segs.text: - Request by Mayor Martell for Discussion and Action on Town of Medley Issued Credit Cards. Mayor Martell addressed the item and proposed that all Town of Medley issued credit cards be removed. He continued to state that only the following individuals cards would remain, his office, Chief of Police, Engineering, and the Office of the Town Clerk. Finance Director Roy Danziger explained that accountants do not like the usage of credit cards. Councilwoman Ayala stated that this is an ongoing issue since 2019 with continued audit findings and it stems from the Town not having a centralized purchasing system, and departments buying their own supplies goes against the Town Ordinance and the Town was provided until April for compliance. In addition, she addressed the mayor and asked how the Town plans to address the purchasing system. Director Danziger explained that the Town is not told what practices to implement but given recommendations from the State. He continued to emphasize that the procurement policy is not followed at most times when items are approved by council. Town Attorney Arango joined the discussion and explained that many processes can be implemented to take steps towards centralized purchasing. Without further discussion, Mayor Martell then placed a motion as follows, TO REMOVE ALL PREVIOUS TOWN ISSUED CREDIT CARDS FROM ALL DEPARTMENT HEADS WITH THE EXCEPTION OF THE MAYOR, THE CHIEF OF POLICE, THE TOWN ENGINEER, AND THE TOWN CLERK Councilperson Ayala seconded the

segs.head: - First Reading of Ordinance C-462 of the Town of Medley Amending the Budget for the Fiscal Year Beginning October 1, 2021 and Ending September 30, 2022.
votes: Mayor Martell made a motion to adopt Ordinance C-462. Vice-Mayor Pacheco seconded the motion, and the first reading of the ordinance was approved unanimously.
segs.text: - First Reading of Ordinance C-462 of the Town of Medley Amending the Budget for the Fiscal Year Beginning October 1, 2021 and Ending September 30, 2022. Finance Director Roy Danziger addressed the Town Council and explained the factors that required a budget amendment such as loan consolidation payments, the sale of the surplus property in the amount of 5.7 million dollars, and the special assessment district created to start collecting in the 2022 tax roll and a$ 1 million dollar surplus for the Building and Zoning department. After a brief discussion, Mayor Martell made a motion to adopt Ordinance C-462. Vice-Mayor Pacheco seconded the motion, and the first reading of the ordinance was approved unanimously. The next item of business was discussed and acted upon as follows,

segs.head: - Discussion on the Proposed Budget for the Fiscal Year October 1, 2022 through September 30, 2023.
segs.text: - Discussion on the Proposed Budget for the Fiscal Year October 1, 2022 through September 30, 2023. Finance Director Roy Danziger began the discussion on the proposed budget for the Fiscal Year beginning October 1, 2022, through September 30, 2023 by announcing the goal of the meeting which was to address the budget including making changes and giving instructions on certain items in addition to setting the tentative millage rate so that it is filed to the County and the state. Director Danziger continued to explain that, taken into consideration the proposed millage rate of 3.2 mills and the projected assessed property value,there would be a projected revenue shortage of$695,000 dollars for FY 2022-2023. Mr. Danziger continued to address a list of items for discussion and possible action including a presentation (see the attached) of the budget report for said fiscal year. Director Danziger also stated that the assessed property value had increase by fifteen percent according to the DR-420 form. The budget items proposed as presented and discussed as follows:

segs.head: - Sale of Parcel B Property.
segs.text: - Sale of Parcel B Property. The proposed budget reflected the sale of a portion of the Parcel B property leaving the attached parcel of land for future Town projects. Vice-Mayor Pacheco expressed his disagreement and stated that after discussing potential uses for the property, it was never intended for the land to be sold. Mayor Martell explained that after having not received interested developers for the intended senior care facility, he believes it is a better strategy to sell the property with the condition that the respective buyer develops a senior care facility committing a portion of the facility to Medley residents.

segs.head: - No raises for non-union employees.
segs.text: - No raises for non-union employees. Vice-Mayor Pacheco expressed his disagreement and circulated a proposed estimate that included the following financial options. . Option 1- 3% increase for all employees except police officers totaling $ 315,000. . Option 2-3%increase for all employees except police officers and salaried employees totaling $ 224,000. Director Roy Danziger stated that a final decision could be made at the first budget public hearing. Town Clerk Victoria Martinez took a moment and announced that the first budget public hearing is scheduled to be held on Monday September 12, 2022 at 5:15 pm and the second and last public hearing is scheduled for Wednesday September 21 also at 5:15 pm.

segs.head: - New Special Revenue Fund.
segs.text: - New Special Revenue Fund. Director Danziger continued the presentation on the proposed budget for FY22-23 and discussed the creation of a new special revenue fund for the building department that created a venue to keep the department's revenues and expenses separately.

segs.head: - Water Budget.
segs.text: - Water Budget. Director Danziger explained that sewer costs have been significantly reduced which have provided savings to the estimated budgeted amounts. Director Danziger further stated that improvements to the sewer system have also provided for reductions in the sewer repairs and if improvements continue, reduction of sewer rates may be feasible in the future.

segs.head: - Stormwater Budget Director Danziger explained that user fees are collected by Miami-Dade County through the tax roll which provides for a substantial reduction in the professional fees previously paid for this matter.
segs.text: - Stormwater Budget Director Danziger explained that user fees are collected by Miami-Dade County through the tax roll which provides for a substantial reduction in the professional fees previously paid for this matter. The next order of business was discussed and acted upon as follows,

segs.head: - Discussion on the Proposed Tentative Millage Rate Based Upon the Certification of Taxable Value of Real and Personal Property Within the Town of Medley for the Fiscal Year October 1, 2022,through September 30, 2023. A brief discussion was held on setting the tentative millage rate emphasizing the pledge to Miami- Dade County to lower the millage rate for the annexation application process.
votes: Vice-Mayor Pacheco made a motion as follows, "TO SET THE PROPOSED TOWN OF MEDLEY AD VALOREM TAX OPERATING MILLAGE LEVY RATE AT 3.200 MILLS FOR FY 2022- 2023." Councilwoman Pacheco seconded the motion, and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: - Discussion on the Proposed Tentative Millage Rate Based Upon the Certification of Taxable Value of Real and Personal Property Within the Town of Medley for the Fiscal Year October 1, 2022,through September 30, 2023. A brief discussion was held on setting the tentative millage rate emphasizing the pledge to Miami- Dade County to lower the millage rate for the annexation application process. Vice-Mayor Pacheco made a motion as follows, "TO SET THE PROPOSED TOWN OF MEDLEY AD VALOREM TAX OPERATING MILLAGE LEVY RATE AT 3.200 MILLS FOR FY 2022- 2023." Councilwoman Pacheco seconded the motion, and it was carried unanimously. Since there was no further business to discuss Mayor Martell made a motion to adjourn the meeting. Councilperson Ayala seconded the motion, and the meeting was adjourned at 7:17 pm on July 21, 2022. Victoria ine RP, CMC, Town Clerk oberto artell, Mayor

votes: Vice-Mayor Pacheco placed a motion to approve Add-On items 13(A)5, 13(A)6 and 13(A)7 and the removal of items 13(A)3 and 13(A)4 as presented. Councilperson Ayala seconded the motion, and the meeting's agenda was carried unanimously.

segs.head: - Ceremonial Check Presentation to the Town of Medley by Florida Representative Tom Fabricio.
segs.text: - Ceremonial Check Presentation to the Town of Medley by Florida Representative Tom Fabricio. Florida State Representative Tom Fabricio from District 103 and Mr. Brian Avila then approached the Council and stated that with the efforts of Senator Manny Diaz, Representative Alex Rizo, Brian Avila, new Representative David Borrero, and Lobbyist Nelson Diaz, he presented the Town of Medley with a check in the amount of One Million Dollars for Roadway Improvements. The Mayor and Council thanked the gentleman for their efforts. The Mayor then announced the following item to be discussed and it was acted upon as follows,

segs.head: - Discussion and Action on the Appointment of One (1) Community Service Aid Position for the Town of Medley Police Department.
votes: Mayor Martell then placed a motion as follows, "TO APPOINT KAMILA SANCHEZ TO THE POSITION OF PART-TIME COMMUNITY SERVICE AID FOR THE TOWN OF MEDLEY POLICE DEPARTMENT." Vice-Mayor Pacheco seconded and the motion it carried unanimously.
segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Appointment of One (1) Community Service Aid Position for the Town of Medley Police Department. Chief Jinete-Said approached the Council to recommend Kamila Sanchez, to the position of part-time community service aid. Mrs. Sanchez then continued to thank the Mayor and Council. Mayor Martell then placed a motion as follows, "TO APPOINT KAMILA SANCHEZ TO THE POSITION OF PART-TIME COMMUNITY SERVICE AID FOR THE TOWN OF MEDLEY POLICE DEPARTMENT." Vice-Mayor Pacheco seconded and the motion it carried unanimously. Mayor Martell then opened the meeting for public comment and employee Niurka Castro, from the Building and Zoning Department approached the podium and addressed the Mayor and Council. Ms. Castro explained how item 13(A)4 was originally meant to be her appointment to the Building and Zoning/License Clerk III position,but she was told that she did not meet the minimum requirements for the position and was not allowed to discuss the matter further with the Mayor. Ms. Castro further explained how she had been transferred from her receptionist position to the building department without prior knowledge or consent, and since then was appointed to Building and Zoning/License Clerk II position as discussed and promised by the Mayor. She explained that she did not meet the minimum requirements at the time for the Clerk II position, but at the discretion of the Town and taking into consideration her education of a bachelor's degree she was promoted. segs.head: - Ordinance C-460 of The Town of Medley, Florida Amending Section 62-38 (F)(1)of The Town Code; Providing For Incorporation of Recitals; Providing For Severability; Providing For Inclusion In The Code;Providing For Conflict And Repealer;Providing For An Effective Date.
votes: Councilperson Ayala placed a motion to approve Ordinance C-460 on first reading. Mayor Martell seconded the motion, and it carried unanimously.
segs.text: - Ordinance C-460 of The Town of Medley, Florida Amending Section 62-38 (F)(1)of The Town Code; Providing For Incorporation of Recitals; Providing For Severability; Providing For Inclusion In The Code;Providing For Conflict And Repealer;Providing For An Effective Date. Once again, Alexander David approached the Council and explained that the proposed Ordinance is to amend the Town code to allow for (8) billboards to a property, whereas it was previously permitted to have (6). The second part of the amendment would allow for the billboards to be moved as long as they stay within the property. Building and Zoning Director William Diaz, clarified that he has no additional input on the matter because Mr. David's firm are the experts in Zoning matters, but he did assure the Council that the Building Department will ensure that the billboards will be permitted per Florida Building Code requirements. Without further discussion, Councilperson Ayala placed a motion to approve Ordinance C-460 on first reading. Mayor Martell seconded the motion, and it carried unanimously.

Councilwoman Ayala addressed the Town Attorney for clarification,and Town Attorney Pizzi explained that there is nothing being changed in the current procurement code, thus it will remain as is. segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Cold Lunch Program. Vice-Mayor Pacheco began the discussion by explaining that he has had a myriad of residents complaining about picking up their cold lunch program sandwiches at Lakeside Retirement Park. He then proposed to move the program to the Medley Municipal Services Facilities (MMSF) and allow residents to drive up to pick up their lunches. Meal Program director Fatima Fuentes approached the Council and expressed how there was a previous attempt to do the cold lunch program at Town hall,but it did not work out for multiple reasons. Nonetheless, director Fuentes expressed that if it is the will of the council to change the location, she will do as instructed with her staff Director Fuentes also explained that there are public health safety requirements such as the refrigeration of the milk that is distributed to each household. Councilwoman Ayala agreed that the Town is required to comply with food safety regulations, or it could cause a public safety issue. A brief discussion was then held to discuss the logistics of relocating the program,and having it operated from the 2nd floor training room or from the garage as proposed by director Fuentes. Consequently, Vice-Mayor Pacheco then placed a motion as follows, "TO MOVE THE COLD LUNCH PROGRAM TO THE MEDLEY MUNICIPAL SERVICES FACILITY FOR RESIDENT PICK UP EFFECTIVE JULY 16, 2022" Councilwoman Pacheco seconded the motion, and the votes were cast as follows, Vice-Mayor Ivan Pacheco- Yes Cou

Therefore,he wished to discuss it at this meeting and called Mr. Corzo to the podium to discuss the matter. OR 1 0 _'' June 21, 2022 Honorable Mayor Martell and Members of the Town Council Medley, Florida Dear Mayor Martell and Members of the Town Council: I'm pleased to present you the Capital Improvement Plan (CIP) for the fiscal years 2022-2026. The CIP serves as a long-range planning tool used to help the Town match revenues with major capital needs over a 5-year period. The projects in the CIP are derived from the Town's Capital Assessment Program, Public requests, Departmental requests/recommendations,Town's Utilities Master Plans, and other economic development needs. A summary version of the CIP was provided with a recommended budget and fiscal year 2023 projects. Subsequent fiscal year projects are unfunded and presented for planning purposes only. As a result of the Town's success in recent applications for Federal and State grant opportunities, fiscal year 2023 includes a large list of projects with grant commitments. Major Factors Impacting Capital Planning Revenue: All budgets are constrained by available revenues. Capital projects are prioritized so that available funds are allocated based on need, Council priority, and their impact on service provision. Therefore, Vice Mayor Pacheco stated that he will adjourn after the discussion and action of item A. Vice | Mayor Pacheco then placed a motion to adopt the meeting s agenda. Town Clerk Victoria Martinez asked, for clarification, if the intent was to table or withdraw item B, noticed as follows,

segs.head: - Discussion and Action on the Town Engineer s Proposed Professional Services Agreement.
segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Town Engineer s Proposed Professional Services Agreement. Vice Mayor Pacheco reiterated that he would adjourn and remove himself from the meeting and then asked Town Attorney Michael Pizzi to clarify further. Town attorney Pizzi explained that without Vice-Mayor Pacheco s attendance, quorum would be lost, and the Town would no longer be able to conduct the public meeting. Councilperson Ayala stated that the Council has had workshops with the previous Town attorneys and former ethics department s director Robert Meyers as well as previous Town attorney Steve Helfman where they clarified that under the Robert s Rules of Order, if a commissioner attends a meeting, they have an obligation to vote on the item and if there is a conflict then they can abstain, providing written reasoning for abstaining. Town attorney Pizzi then referred to a recent occurrence when Town s elected officials and staff attended a Miami-Dade County meeting, and several commissioners left the meeting losing quorum resulting in the meeting to end. Thus, Mr. Pizzi continued and stated that his legal opinion on the matter is that business cannot be conducted with less than three councilmembers in attendance. Without further discussion, Mayor Martell seconded the motion to adopt the meeting s agenda, and councilperson Ayala stated that he would recuse himself from the meeting and exited the council chambers. Quorum was lost and the meeting was adjourned at 5:22 pm on June 21, 20

Figure 2-1: Sanderson District Limits Capital Projects & Economic Development Department Funding Methodology Report Capital Assessment District 05-Sanderson Town of Medley Within this area, NW South River Drive, NW 118th Way and NW 117th Way are Town of Medley R/Ws. The existing waterway C-6 Canal (maintained by the South Florida Water Management District) borders the northeasterly edge of the area. Following the review of the Florida Department of Environmental Protection (FDEP) Contamination Locator Map GIS database, no contaminated properties were observed within the study limits. However, there is an FDEP cleanup site (ID 982083115) within the limits of this District located at 10300 NW 121st Way (Duke Realty Limit Partnership). According to the FEMA Flood Zoning map, part of the Sanderson District is classified as FEMA Flood Zone AH with a base flood elevation (BFE) of 7.00 FT (NGVD). Among the R/W facilities within the District, NW 117th Way and NW 118th Way appears to be above BFE, being on FEMA Flood Zone X, which represents minimal flood hazard. On the other hand, NW South River Drive is partially located within FEMA Flood Zone AH with a BFE of 7 FT (NGVD). segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Proposed Amendment to the Town of Medley Capital Improvement Plan FY 2022-2026. Assistant Director Manny Perez approached the Council and presented the proposed amendments to the FY 2022 Capital improvement plan, and explained that a workshop will need to be scheduled to discuss the 2023 fiscal year. The proposed changes are to reduce the 14-million-dollar budget to 8.4 million dollars because some projects are not set to commence until the 2023 Fiscal Year. Finance Director Roy Danziger approached the Council and asked for clarification about whether or not the remaining 7 million dollars are anticipated to be spent within the last three months of the 2022 fiscal year. He stated that the all a a ia a ia Town is already amending the budget per the requirement for a debt refinancing, which will be presented to the Council in July, and the amendment will require to reflect what has been done throughout the year. Assistant Director Perez explained that the numbers are determined by contracts, and although the projected expenditures may not be used in the current year the department may receive bills for payment on undetermined amounts at any time. Mayor Martell instructed staff to meet and then present their proposal at a Council workshop to discuss the capital improvement plan in mid-June.
