segs.head: - Discussion and Action on the Salary Study and Gender Analysis for the Town of Medley Prepared by Evergreen Solutions, LLC.
votes: Mayor Martell then placed a motion as follows, TO ACCEPT THE FINDINGS BY EVERGREEN SOLUTIONS FOR THE SALARY STUDY AND GENDER ANALYSIS, Vice Mayor Pacheco seconded, and it carried unanimously.
segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Salary Study and Gender Analysis for the Town of Medley Prepared by Evergreen Solutions, LLC. Town Attorney Michael Pizzi began the discussion by explaining that there are two operative points that he would like to focus on and reflected on page 28 of the study. Mr. Pizzi read the differences in salaries in this instance may be more indicative of the level of complexity of the position, role, responsibility, and salary potential of each classification. Attorney Pizzi further stated that the study also states that Based on the results of the market survey, when comparing operational level, essential skills and education/certifications, the Town offers a competitive rate of pay . Attorney Pizzi concluded that there is no evidence of any gender base discrimination in the Town of Medley salary levels according to the data. He further stated that the report states that different individuals have different levels of requirements, education, experience, and duties therefore have different salaries. Furthermore, Mr. Pizzi also concluded that Medley when comparing salaries to other cities has a competitive rate regardless of the gender. He continued to state that the study shows that there are twenty- one people with different experience levels doing entirely different unrelated positions, and the salaries are different as expected of different job titles, concluding that there is no gender discrimination. Town Attorney Lillian Arango explained that this is the first of two necessary hearings for the adoption of the above-mentioned resolution. The second hearing will be presented on April 4, 2022, and fourteen days prior a notice will be posted by the Office of the Town Clerk.Building and Zoning director William Diaz approached the podium and explained that the previously approved schedule was in 2015 and since then changes have been made such as the State of Florida prohibiting the request of a job contract between contractors and owners, thus the current fees are based on the job cost provided for by the contractor. The new schedule will allow to calculate permit fees based on the square footage of the construction. Also,it was noted that on page 21 for the building department fee schedule there was an error for the cost to change the business name, address or owner and the correct amount is to be $25.00. segs.text: - Request by Mayor Martell for Discussion and Action on the Town of Medley Gender Analysis and Compensation Study. Labor Counsel Caroline Saiz was present and stated that there are two options at this time,the gender analysis with a cost of$4,000.00, or evergreen solutions can perform both a gender analysis and a comprehensive analysis of the compensation for all the positions for a total cost of$14,000.00. segs.text: - Request by Mayor Martell for Discussion and Action on Tobie Wilson Park Structural Concerns. Director Diaz continued to state that said property has no information with the Miami-Dade County Property Appraiser, thus it was not built with permits or registered as an existing building with the County. It was noted that the building was constructed in the 1970's requiring at this time a 40-year recertification, as well as a structural study. Councilperson Ayala asked for clarification on the intent for this item and Mayor Martell proceeded to recommend that a new three-story building be built to replace the Tobie Wilson park,in compliance with the Florida Building Code to be used as a hurricane shelter. It was also stated that once a repair exceeds 25%of the structure, it is then required to bring the building's structure up to the 2022 Florida Building Code. segs.text: - Discussion and Action on Town of Medley Pension Benefits I Finance Director Roy Danziger approached the Council to request permission to amend the Town of Medley general pension plan. He explained that currently the plans benefit is calculated based on the employees last five consecutive years of employment,and his proposal is to amend the policy for it to be calculated based on the employees five highest earning years in a ten-year period rather than consecutive years.The intent is to assist a long-term employee,that earned less monies one year for an injury in which workers compensation is received, and that year is being considered in the average calculation for the retirement benefit. segs.text: - Ordinance C-457 of the Town of Medley, Florida, Amending the Official Zoning Map of the Town by Amending the Zoning Designation of Parcels of Land Generally Located North of NW 90th Street and East of NW 107th Avenue Consisting of Approximately 258.16 Acres, Currently Designated R-1 One-Family District to M-1 Industrial District, as More Particularly Depicted in the Map Attached as Exhibit"A"Hereto, and Legally Described in Exhibit `B" Attached Hereto; and Providing for an Effective Date (Area A Rezoning Central/Lakeside). Councilperson Ayala asked for clarification on the term FLUM, which Mr. Hickey clarified to be the acronym used for the term Future Land Use Map. Mr. Hickey continued to explain that the underlining land use is Industrial for the parcel of land presented, but the Zoning is R1, which would require the developer to change the use. It was also stated that if land is submerged, then the property can be filled and developed after getting a site plan approved to redevelop it for industrial purposes. Thus,the purpose of the proposed Ordinance is to change the R-1 zoning to M-1 zoning to match the current use of the properties highlighted. Without further discussion Mayor Martell placed a motion to approve Ordinance C-457 on first reading. Councilperson Ayala seconded the motion, and it carried unanimously.

segs.head: - Discussion and Action on the Flex Time Off for Salaried Employees.
segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Flex Time Off for Salaried Employees. Mayor Martell addressed the item explaining his intent which was to both remove the flex time off benefit afforded to the exempt employees and removing the punching in and out process for exempt employees. Mayor Martell further explained that after inquiring the punching in and out process of 21 cities, it was determined that no other city had salary employees punching in and out. Director Roy Danziger approached the Council and clarified for councilwoman Ayala that salary employees are paid for the job and are expected to work even outside of regularly scheduled hours,thus working on a weekend does not afford that employee to take a day off during the week. Councilwoman Ayala expressed that she was not being provided enough information to make a decision on the employee matter,and would like additional information from either legal, or labor, but unfortunately labor counsel was not present. Director Danziger then clarified that the current flex time off benefit is a policy where exempt employees working six consecutive hours on a day that is not their regularly schedule workday, would allow exempt employees to take a full day off within a thirty (30) day period and the mayor's proposal is to remove this benefit. segs.head: - Discussion and Action on the Town of Medley Continued and Revised 2020 Annexation Application with Miami-Dade County.
segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Town of Medley Continued and Revised 2020 Annexation Application with Miami-Dade County. Vice Mayor Pacheco began the discussion by asking for clarification on the resolutions adopted by Miami Springs and Virginia Gardens. Town Attorney Michael Pizzi explained that although resolutions had been adopted including mitigation fees, that fee would be eliminated once the ordinance went before the County commission. Mr. Pizzi continued to explain that the County initially urged the Town to adopt a resolution entering into an interlocal agreement that would require the Town of Medley to pay Miami-Dade County a mitigation fee close to $600,000 a year for seven years, and that the County after adoption would then remove the requirement for the mitigation fee. Mr. Pizzi continued to explain that he was not in agreement with adopting said resolution and after discussion with the County, it has been agreed to modify the resolution. Therefore, the Town may adopt a resolution entering into an interlocal agreement with Miami- Dade County eliminating the mitigation fee in its entirety. Mr. Pizzi explained how he compared agreements of other cities to ensure that the Town of Medley was getting a fair agreement. Mr. Pizzi continued to congratulate the Mayor and Council and further explained the process for finalizing the annexation. segs.text: - Update on the Town of Medley Continued and Revised Application for Annexation Submitted to Miami-Dade County. Town Attorney Pizzi began the discussion by explaining that the Town, to comply with the requirements for the annexation, would not only adopt an ordinance which would change the boundaries of the Town, but the Town would also enter into an inter local agreement as Miami Springs, and Virginia Gardens to address zoning and other related matters. Additionally, Town attorney Pizzi stated that regarding Medley s application, there is one parcel of land where a portion would be annexed, and the Town of Medley was required to have a survey performed with permission of the property owner as well as have the property appraiser s office perform an appraisal of the land. Furthermore, when approved Miami-Dade County recommends that Medley make a $86,000.00 payment for a bond every year and a mitigation payment of $517,000.00 a year for a total of seven years. Councilperson Ayala recommended that a workshop be done to explain further, and Mr. Pizzi agreed that educating the Council on annexation would be a great idea. Since there was no other business to address, Vice-Mayor Pacheco placed a motion to adjourn the meeting. The motion was carried unanimously, and the meeting was adjourned at 7:29pm. (Folio No. 22-3003-033-0053) James Hickey,consulting Town Planner,and Paul Hernandez representative for the applicant approached the podium. Mr. Hickey briefly explained that the applicant performs engine testing,and the Town Code currently has a limit of 80-A decimal level,but through multiple tests they have determined that they go over the decimals allowed for in the Town Code and would like to formally request a variance allowing an increase to 90-A decimals. Mr. Hernandez also explained and clarified by giving examples to sounds that would be equivalent to 90-A decimals and how it is unlikely that it would be heard by neighboring businesses or the residential area. Additionally, Mr. Hernandez noted that the Town, to date, has not received any complaints while IAero has been conducting its business. Councilwoman Ayala seconded the motion, and it carried unanimously.

segs.text: - Resolution C-2029 Approving and Amending the Town of Medley Building Fee Schedule. Town Attorney Pizzi explained that according to Florida Statue the Building Department can only generate enough revenue to pay for departmental needs and not generate a surplus,but be self-contained as surpluses cannot be transferred to general funds or used for other departments.Attorney Pizzi further stated that if funds are generated in excess of what is required,the Town must either return the funds or amend its fee schedule. In addition, Mr. Pizzi stated that after discussions with the finance director, building department director, and discussions with other cities, it was explained that if your budget shows a surplus for over five years then the consistent surplus would require an amendment to the fee schedule.Therefore Mr. Pizzi presented the following resolution proposing a ten percent(10%)decrease across the board for all building department fees, which he believes will not result in a short fall and alleviate the concerns of generating continuous surpluses. Without further discussion, Mayor Martell placed a motion to approve resolution C-2029. Vice-Mayor Pacheco seconded the motion, and the motion carried unanimously.

Discussion on the letter of resignation presented by the Building and Zoning Director William Diaz Councilperson Ayala addressed Director Diaz, and he then approached the podium. Mayor Martell expressed his disagreement to hear Director Diaz's comments on the matter and asked him not to speak publicly. Additionally, Councilwoman Ayala asked the Mayor if silencing the employees was correct, and she asked if she could request for Mr. Diaz to speak. Mayor Martell explained that Mr. Diaz could not speak,and the employees speak out of line when he has always had an open-door policy for them to come discuss concerns. Again, Director Diaz approached the podium and requested to speak on the mater. Mayor Martell then instructed Lieutenant Jinete to remove Mr. Diaz from the chambers if he attempted to publicly speak without permission. Councilwoman Ayala addressed the Town Attorney and stated that we live in a Democracy,and it is the job of an elected official to listen to the public even if the comments are disagreeable. Councilwoman Ayala further stated that it is unfortunate that the Town is encouraging an environment where employees cannot even speak, which is wrong. Additionally,Councilwoman Ayala asked Attorney Pizzi that since the administration did away with the Human Resources position, what would happen if employees got to point where they fear speaking to the Mayor, do not feel protected and are being urged to resign or be publicly fired which is wrong. segs.text: - Presentation and Recognition of the Police Department Officer of the Bid Award. Lieutenant German Gutierrez approached the Council and announced that officer Luis Rivera was the recipient of the Officer of the Bid Award from July through December 2022. He continued to state that in October of 2022 officer Rivera received the Life Saving Award for assisting another officer in saving the life of a wounded victim. Moreover, officer Rivera assisted the Seminole Police Department in locating a federal wanted individual. It was noted that aside from officer Rivera performing his official duties, he is also a part of the Police Department s social media unit and serves as a public information officer. Therefore, for his display of teamwork, professionalism, and utmost loyalty to the department, officer Luis Rivera was awarded with the Officer of the Bid Award. Officer Luis Rivera then approached to thank the Police Department s Command staff, his fellow officers, and the Town council for acknowledging his hard work.

segs.text: - Presentation and Recognition of the Police Department Chief's Award. Sergeant Louis Ponce was awarded the Chief s award and was recognized for his outstanding work ethics, dedication to the department s accreditation process and for his devotion to continued training efforts. Sergeant Ponce approached the Council and stated that the award was a recognition to every member of the team whose efforts helped accomplish the accreditation. Additionally, sergeant Ponce expressed his gratitude to the Chief of Police for her leadership and vision, the Mayor and Council for their unwavering support, and his colleges for their hard work towards this accomplishment.

segs.head: - Presentation and Recognition of the Police Department Officer of the Year Award.
segs.text: - Presentation and Recognition of the Police Department Officer of the Year Award. Officer Omar Galvan was awarded the Officer of the Year Award and was recognized for his exemplary performance throughout the year. It was sated that he has consistently been the most productive officer in arrests, traffic enforcements, and self-initiative activities. It was also stated that in October 2022 officer Galvan received the Life Saving Award for his immediate action in applying a tourniquet technique to a wounded victim which would have otherwise perished and on the same day, he continued to locate a fleeing armed subject that with his efforts, was detained. It was also stated that these occasions are only an example of his continued hard work and efforts, thus earning him the title of Officer of the Year. Officer Omar Galvan then approached the Council and expressed his gratitude towards all his mentors and colleagues as well as the Mayor and Council. segs.head: - Discussion and Action for the Request to Notice Two (2) Utilities Laborer Positions for the Utilities Department.
votes: Mayor Martell made a motion to approve the request for two utilities laborer position. Councilwoman Pacheco seconded the motion, and the votes were cast as follows, Mayor Roberto Martell - Yes Vice-Mayor Edgar Ayala - Yes Councilperson Lizelh Ayala- Yes Councilperson Ivan Pacheco- No Councilperson Karina Pacheco- Yes The motion was carried by majority of vote.
segs.text: - Discussion and Action for the Request to Notice Two (2) Utilities Laborer Positions for the Utilities Department. Director Jorge Soto approached the Council and explained that the two requested positions were to partially fill vacancies in the department since four positions had been vacant in the recent years. Councilperson Pacheco expressed his disagreement with the request since a hiring freeze had recently been implemented and he did not wish to open said freeze. Vice Mayor asked for clarification on the filling of the vacant positions, whereas Director Soto explained that the applicants need a high school diploma or equivalent to obtain their license through the State of Florida and be qualified for the positions. Vice-Mayor Ayala also addressed the hiring freeze and asked Town Attorney Pizzi whether the hiring freeze was in effect since hirings had occurred after its adoption. Mayor Martell explained that the request was for four employees, but director Soto agreed to the hiring of two, to allow for the minimum number of hires for departmental function. Councilwoman Ayala interjected and stated that it is important to provide employees when a department is deficient because that is how the Town will continue to run efficiently and stated her support for the item. Additionally, Councilwoman Ayala also stated that the hire will help the department because working understaffed is difficult. Councilwoman Ayala also thanked director Soto for his willingness to compromise.

segs.text: - Ordinance C-473 Amending Chapter 2 Administration by Creating Article VI Social Services Programs District to Create Definitions, Registration Requirements, and Enforcement; Providing for Conflicts; Providing for Severability; Providing for Codification; and Providing for an Effective Date. Councilwoman Rodriguez inquired about language in page 2 which read who reside at properties that exist in the Town of Medley on the day of the passage of the Ordinance... its correlation with college students that are studying out of Town and whether the proposed language would affect them. Attorney Pizzi explained that the purpose of this Ordinance is to make sure that everybody who has been living in the Town of Medley and every property that has ever participated in the Town of Medley social services programs do not become affected and thus, will continue to participate in each program. Mr. Pizzi further explained that the proposed legislation would be for new developments that have not demonstrated needs and are not currently part of the Town as of now. segs.text: - Request by Councilperson Pacheco for Discussion and Action on the Town of Medley Community Pool Operations. Councilperson Pacheco began the discussion by stating that he has received complaints for the last couple of months about the pool being closed. Councilperson Pacheco further stated that the pool has been closed since September and he had circulated cost estimates for lifeguard services to expand the current hours of operations and explained that the Town already pays monthly maintenance expenses for the heated pool. Mayor Martell explained that the expense associated with opening the community pool all year round would be 128,000 thousand dollars per year which is not cost effective for the Town and that, according to the visitor logs that were also circulated, there was not enough attendance on Fridays. Thus, Mayor Martell proposed to try and extend the current operating hours to weekends only and instructed finance director Charmain Parchment to obtain a cost estimate for lifeguard services for the proposed weekend only schedule. Councilwoman Rodriguez joined the discussion and stated that weather starts getting hot in the month of March and that whatever decision is taken, the Town needs to do a better job at informing the residents of the pool schedule. segs.text: - An Ordinance of the Town of Medley, Florida, Providing an Amendment to Ordinance C- 455 Amending Section 2-86 of the Code, Settlement; Disposition of All Collected Fines And Liens to Read Mitigation of Fines, Penalties and Liens ; Establishing Procedures and Guidelines for the Mitigation of Code Enforcement Fines, Penalties and Liens; Providing for Codification; Providing for Severability; Providing for Conflicts; and Providing for an Effective Date. Town Attorney Michael A. Pizzi explained that the methodology in which Code enforcement fines are assessed and how at times daily accrual of fines surpass the value of the property, thus the cost becomes exuberant and unreasonable for the property owners. Mr. Pizzi further stated that many cities have passed legislation capping fee amounts and that prior to adopting Ordinance C-455, the Town had the ability to hear a property s owner circumstances and determine if there was just cause in not curing the violation by the compliance deadline. Therefore, the ordinance presented proposes to cap the Town of Medley Code Compliance fines at the assessed amount of One Hundred and Fifty Thousand dollars. Vice-Mayor Ayala proposed to amend the proposed capped amount and to lower the cap to One Hundred Thousand dollars to which it was agreed upon. segs.text: - Resolution C-2062 Directing the Town Attorney to Initiate the Process to Amend the Town Charter to Remove Article VIII of the Town of Medley Charter; Providing for Implementation; and Providing for an Effective Date. Councilwoman Ayala expressed concerns with how vague the current resolution was presented and stated that removing article VIII is removing a supervisor s right to have representation through a board, thus finds it troublesome. Councilwoman Ayala also stated that she is not in agreement with the removal of Article VII, further stating that employees have a right to a due process. Additionally, Councilwoman Ayala asked for the specific purpose of the item being brought up but expressed that an entire charter review would be healthy. However, the proposed resolution only addresses one section of the Town charter. Mr. Pizzi explained that members of the Council have expressed that the administrative review board process served no purpose because ultimately the matter comes back to the Town Council for a vote, and in his experience these administrative review board processes do not do anyone any favors and are useless delays because the process results in the same body of the board that dec

Additionally, she explained that there are currently 62 residents receiving services through the Town s the medical transportation program. Councilwoman Ayala expressed concerns with the Council s inclination to waive fees and accommodate business needs while considering cutting expenses in residential programs. Councilwoman Ayala also explained that although STS is a program available for all Miami-Dade County residents, there are many practices such as single riding, long wait times and commute times that would drastically change, making a difficult transition for the residents. Nonetheless, Councilwoman Ayala explained that she is not against exploring alternative options if the Uber medical services are too costly. Ultimately, Councilwoman Ayala stated that if the Town can accommodate the businesses, then the Town should also accommodate the Town s elderly community. segs.head: - Request by Councilperson Pacheco for Discussion and Action on the Creation of Policy for Limitations of Town of Medley Donations Councilperson Pacheco began by asking for clarification whether there is a policy on donation limitation.
segs.text: - Request by Councilperson Pacheco for Discussion and Action on the Creation of Policy for Limitations of Town of Medley Donations Councilperson Pacheco began by asking for clarification whether there is a policy on donation limitation. Town Clerk Martinez explaining that although no formal policy exists there has always been the practice of a $500.00 dollar limitation. Vice-Mayor Ayala explained that if the Town is approached to help in a big endeavor and is limited to only donate $500.00 then the Town looks frugal and does not agree on limitations when there could be needy causes. Councilwoman Ayala included that she believed the Town can be responsible while still being generous when it comes to the residents, and explained how the Town was able to send young students to a science competition that exposes them to STEM careers and medicine, which is harder for people with minority backgrounds or low incomes to have access to these careers. She further stated that the Town was able provide access to those young residents due to the donation approved by Council. Thus, expressed disagreement with establishing a cap amount. Councilperson Pacheco then placed a motion as follows, TO APPROVE A MAXIMUM LIMITATION OF $500.00 DOLLARS PER TOWN DONATION, ALLOWING FOR THE COUNCIL TO APPROVE A HIGHER DONATION AMOUNT IF ANY COUNCILMEMBER PRESENTS A CAUSE WITH NEED FOR THE SAME Vice-Mayor Ayala seconded the motion, and the votes were cast as follows, Mayor Roberto Martell Yes Vice-Mayor Ed

segs.head: - Discussion and Action on the Pending Town of Medley Annexation Application.
segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Pending Town of Medley Annexation Application. Town Attorney Michael Pizzi congratulated the Town Council and Town residents and stated that after twenty years the annexation had finally been approved and further explained that the only annexation application approved was the one submitted by the Town of Medley. It was noted that a new interlocal agreement has been approved with language requiring four years of mitigation payments, and there will be a meeting with the County to confirm a start date for said payments. Mr. Pizzi also explained that police service has been provided to annexed areas since the initial approval of the annexation application. It was also clarified that the mitigation payment is set to be $517,000 dollars for the first year and increased by a percentage for a span of four years. Furthermore, after meeting with the County the Town attorney will come back to Council to report the details of the transitionary plan agreed upon for all services such as utilities, public works, etcetera.

segs.head: - Discussion on the Proposed Budget for the Fiscal Year October 1, 2023, Through September 30, 2024.
segs.text: - Discussion on the Proposed Budget for the Fiscal Year October 1, 2023, Through September 30, 2024. Finance Director Charmaine Parchment discussed the Town's preliminary 2023-2024 budget and announced the 2023 certified taxable property value to be $ 5,192,600,352. Director Parchment also stated that the taxable property value included the value of the recently annexed properties and that the change in taxable property value from 2022 is $ 1,987,358,188. Director Parchment also discussed the preliminary 2023-2024 general fund's revenues and expenses as well as the budget timeline for fiscal year 2023-2024. Town Clerk Victoria Martinez took a moment and announced that the first budget public hearing is scheduled to be held on Monday September 11, 2023 at 6:00 pm and the second and last public hearing is scheduled for Tuesday September 26, 2023 also at 6:00 pm.

segs.text: B. DUTIES AND EXPECTATIONS: Managers and Supervisors shall be responsible for preventing acts of discrimination and harassments and utilizing this policy in the event such conduct is reported. These responsibilities include: 1. Expressing strong disapproval of all forms of discrimination, harassment and retaliation; 2. Monitoring the work environment on a continuous basis for signs of discrimination, harassment and/or retaliation; 3. Stopping any observed acts of possible discrimination, harassment or retaliation by taking the appropriate steps to immediately intervene in the observed behavior; 4. Immediately reporting any observed or reported acts of possible discrimination, harassment and/or retaliation to the next level supervisor or manager and/or to the Town s EO Officer; and 5. Providing immediate assistance to any Town employee who reports discrimination, harassment and/or retaliation. A manager or supervisor s failure to carry out these responsibilities shall be considered in any evaluation or promotional decision and may be grounds for discipline, up to and including termination. All Town employees shall also be responsible for adhering to this Policy and assisting in the prevention of discrimination and harassment by: 1. Refraining from participating in, or encouraging actions that could be perceived as discrimination, harassment and/or retaliation; 2. Harassment can also include, for example, offensive or derogatory remarks about a person's transgender status or gender transition. In Bostock vy. Clayton County, Georgia, No. 17-1618 (S. Ct. June 15, 2020),[1] the Supreme Court held that firing individuals because of their sexual orientation or transgender status violates Title VII s prohibition on discrimination because of sex. The Court reached its holding by focusing on the plain text of Title VII. As the Court explained, discrimination based on homosexuality or transgender status necessarily entails discrimination based on sex; the first cannot happen without the second. For example, if an employer fires an employee because she is a woman who is married to a woman, but would not do the same to a man married to a woman, the employer is taking an action because of the employee s sex because the action would not have taken place but for the employee being a woman. segs.head: (5) NATURE OF INFORMATION DISCLOSED.
segs.text: (5) NATURE OF INFORMATION DISCLOSED. The information disclosed under this section must include: (a) Any violation or suspected violation of any federal, state, or local law, rule, or regulation committed by an employee or agent of an agency or independent contractor which creates and presents a substantial and specific danger to the public s health, safety, or welfare. (b) Any act or suspected act of gross mismanagement, malfeasance, misfeasance, gross waste of public funds, suspected or actual Medicaid fraud or abuse, or gross neglect of duty committed by an employee or agent of an agency or independent contractor.

segs.head: (6) TO WHOM INFORMATION DISCLOSED.
segs.text: (6) TO WHOM INFORMATION DISCLOSED. The information disclosed under this section must be disclosed to any agency or federal government entity having the authority to investigate, police, manage, or otherwise remedy the violation or act, including, but not limited to, the Office of the Chief Inspector General, an agency inspector general or the employee designated as agency inspector general under s. 112.3189(1) or inspectors general under s. 20.055, the Florida Commission on Human Relations, and the whistle-blower s hotline created under s. 112.3189. However, for disclosures concerning a local governmental entity, including any regional, county, or municipal entity, special district, community college district, or school district or any political subdivision of any of the foregoing, the information must be disclosed to a chief executive officer as defined in s. 447.203(9) or other appropriate local official. Adverse action against employee for disclosing information of specified nature prohibited; employee remedy and relief.

segs.head: (7) EMPLOYEES AND PERSONS PROTECTED.
segs.text: (7) EMPLOYEES AND PERSONS PROTECTED. This section protects employees and persons who disclose information on their own initiative in a written and signed complaint; who are requested to participate in an investigation, hearing, or other inquiry conducted by any agency or federal government entity; who refuse to participate in any adverse action prohibited by this section; or who initiate a complaint through the whistle-blower s hotline or the hotline of the Medicaid Fraud Control Unit of the Department of Legal Affairs; or employees who file any written complaint to their supervisory officials or employees who submit a complaint to the Chief Inspector General in the Executive Office of the Governor, to the employee designated as agency inspector general under s. 112.3189(1), or to the Florida Commission on Human Relations. The provisions of this section may not be used by a person while he or she is under the care, custody, or control of the state correctional system or, after release from the care, custody, or control of the state correctional system, with respect to circumstances that occurred during any period of incarceration. No remedy or other protection under ss. 112.3187-112.31895 applies to any person who has committed or intentionally participated in committing the violation or suspected violation for which protection under ss. 112.3187-112.31895 is being sought.

(a) Any employee of or applicant for employment with any state agency, as the term state agency is defined ins. 216.011, who is discharged, disciplined, or subjected to other adverse personnel action, or denied employment, because he or she engaged in an activity protected by this section may file a complaint, which complaint must be made in accordance with s. 112.31895. Upon receipt of notice from the Florida Commission on Human Relations of termination of the investigation, the complainant may elect to pursue the administrative remedy available under s. 1 12.31895 or bring a civil action within 180 days after receipt of the notice. (b) Within 60 days after the action prohibited by this section, any local public employee protected by this section may file a complaint with the appropriate local governmental authority, if that authority has established by ordinance an administrative procedure for handling such complaints or has contracted with the Division of Administrative Hearings under s. 120.65 to conduct hearings under this section. The administrative procedure created by ordinance must provide for the complaint to be heard by a panel of impartial persons appointed by the appropriate local governmental authority. segs.head: (9) RELIEF.
segs.text: (9) RELIEF. In any action brought under this section, the relief must include the following: (a) Reinstatement of the employee to the same position held before the adverse action was commenced, or to an equivalent position or reasonable front pay as alternative relief. (b) Reinstatement of the employee s full fringe benefits and seniority rights, as appropriate. (c) Compensation, if appropriate, for lost wages, benefits, or other lost remuneration caused by the adverse action. (d) Payment of reasonable costs, including attorney s fees, to a substantially prevailing employee, or to the prevailing employer if the employee filed a frivolous action in bad faith. (e) Issuance of an injunction, if appropriate, by a court of competent jurisdiction. (f) Temporary reinstatement to the employee s former position or to an equivalent position, pending the final outcome on the complaint, if an employee complains of being discharged in retaliation for a protected disclosure and if a court of competent jurisdiction or the Florida Commission on Human Relations, as applicable under s. 112.31895, determines that the disclosure was not made in bad faith or for a wrongful purpose or occurred after an agency s initiation of a personnel action against the employee which includes documentation of the employee s violation of a disciplinary standard or performance deficiency. segs.head: A.
segs.text: A. Except as provided in Section 6.04, any municipality in the county may adopt, amend, or revoke a charter for its own government or abolish its existence in the following manner. Its governing body shall within 120 days after adopting a resolution or after the certification of a petition of ten percent of the qualified electors of the municipality, draft or have drafted by a method determined by municipal ordinance a proposed charter amendment, revocation, or abolition which shall be submitted to the electors of the municipalities. Unless an election occurs not less than 60 nor more than 120 days after the draft is submitted, the proposal shall be submitted at a special election within that time. The governing body shall make copies of the proposal available to the electors not less that 30 days before the election. Alternative proposals shall be submitted. segs.head: - Request by Councilwoman Ayala for Discussion and Action on the Town of Medley After School Program Educational Resources.
votes: Councilwoman Ayala placed a motion as follows, "TO APPROVE THE PURCHASE (4) IPADS FOR THE AFTERSCHOOL PROGRAM TO BE COMPATIBLE WITH THE SOFTWARE NECESSARY FOR TUTORING SERVICES" Mayor Martell seconded the motion, and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: - Request by Councilwoman Ayala for Discussion and Action on the Town of Medley After School Program Educational Resources. Councilwoman Ayala began the discussion by explaining that the Town's afterschool program has experienced an influx of immigrated students who need to learn the English language. Therefore, Bob Lebron,the afterschool program tutor has been dedicating time to help teach those students the language. Thus, the afterschool program has a demand for additional devices due to the increased number of children in the program and the need to assist both the immigrated and the students already enrolled in the program. Councilwoman Ayala then proposed for the Town to purchase four(4)IPAD's compatible with the software used for the students' learning programs,assigned homework and school assignments. The Council expressed their agreement, and affirmed the Mayor's discretion to follow the Town's protocols for the purchase. Without further discussion, Councilwoman Ayala placed a motion as follows, "TO APPROVE THE PURCHASE (4) IPADS FOR THE AFTERSCHOOL PROGRAM TO BE COMPATIBLE WITH THE SOFTWARE NECESSARY FOR TUTORING SERVICES" Mayor Martell seconded the motion, and it was carried unanimously.

A recap of the Council workshop that had taken place at 4:00 pm was discussed.After discussion,it was determined to apply the same criteria to all resident services programs except for the afterschool program, summer camp program and the start-up grant program.
segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Town of Medley Social Services programs. A recap of the Council workshop that had taken place at 4:00 pm was discussed.After discussion,it was determined to apply the same criteria to all resident services programs except for the afterschool program, summer camp program and the start-up grant program. As previously requested during the Council workshop, Finance Director Charmaine circulated the 2023 Federal Poverty Guidelines reflecting the annual income ranges for households,depending on the family size. Mayor Martell then addressed the intent to implement the federal poverty guidelines to all social services programs. Councilwoman Ayala expressed concerns with implementing these guidelines to children's programs and the Start-Up grant program,therefore she requested they be excluded from the new criteria. Additionally, it was the consensus of the Council to have annual renewals of program's registrations due to the yearly changes of the federal poverty guidelines. The Council was also in agreement to apply the annual renewal of services to the light housekeeping program and for the annual registrations of all programs to be done in March of every year. It was also agreed upon by the Town Council to grandfather all existing program participants under the former criteria. segs.text: - Approval/Corrections of the Minutes of the Regular Council Meeting of April 3, 2023. Vice-Mayor Ayala made a motion to approve the minutes for the April 3, 2023 regular council meeting as presented, and the minutes were adopted unanimously. Mayor Martell then announced the addition of Resolution C-2088 to the Resolutions section of the agenda as item 12(K) and the withdrawal of Resolutions items 12(A) and 12(J) from the night s agenda. In addition, Mayor Martell announced the addition of the following Town of Medley item, - 13(A)4 Discussion and Action of the Town of Medley Medical Bathing Services Program. Councilwoman Ayala also announced the addition of the following item, - 13(A)5 Discussion and Action on the Policies Enforcing the Sports Contribution Program. segs.head: - Ordinance C-467 of the Town of Medley, Florida, Amending Ordinance C-393 by Adding Section 2-146 Lobbying After Employment Extending the Two (2) Years Prohibition to Four (4) Years After Employment; Providing for Conflicts; Providing for Severability; Providing for Codification; and Providing for an Effective Date.
votes: Mayor Martell placed a motion to approve Ordinance C-467 on first reading. Councilwoman Pacheco seconded the motion, and the votes were cast as follows, Mayor Roberto Martell - Yes Vice-Mayor Edgar Ayala - No Councilperson Lizelh Ayala- No Councilperson Ivan Pacheco- Yes Councilperson Karina Pacheco- Yes The motion was carried by majority of vote.
segs.text: - Ordinance C-467 of the Town of Medley, Florida, Amending Ordinance C-393 by Adding Section 2-146 Lobbying After Employment Extending the Two (2) Years Prohibition to Four (4) Years After Employment; Providing for Conflicts; Providing for Severability; Providing for Codification; and Providing for an Effective Date. Mayor Martell opened the meeting for public comment on this matter. It was noted that no public comments were made. Councilwoman Ayala asked for clarification on the language of Miami Dade County conflict of interest ordinance, and Town Attorney Pizzi explained that the County ordinance mandates the prohibition for a period of two years but that the state of Florida had recently amended legislation that changed it to either five or six years. Without further discussion, Mayor Martell placed a motion to approve Ordinance C-467 on first reading. Councilwoman Pacheco seconded the motion, and the votes were cast as follows, Mayor Roberto Martell - Yes Vice-Mayor Edgar Ayala - No Councilperson Lizelh Ayala- No Councilperson Ivan Pacheco- Yes Councilperson Karina Pacheco- Yes The motion was carried by majority of vote. segs.text: - Discussion and Action on Fleet Services for the Town of Medley and the Medley Police Department. Daniel Pacheco, Area Manager, and Abeo Manning, Client Strategy Manager from Enterprise Fleet Management with offices at 5105 Johnson Road Coconut Creek, FL 33073 approached the Council. Mayor Martell explained that his intent is to lease the Town s vehicles to get the most out of the Town s fleet and acquire thirty new vehicles. Mayor Martell further explained that the Town auctioned four vehicles and that Ms. Charmaine Parchment, the Town s finance director, analyzed the financial data from the sale. Councilwoman Ayala asked for a brief overview of the services provided. Mr. Pacheco continued to explain that their company is a total fleet management provider that assists in acquisition, maintenance, fueling and everything related to operating the vehicles. Vice-Mayor Ayala asked for clarification on the cost for leasing the vehicles. Mr. Pacheco explained that it is considered a purchase based on an equity lease structure, a municipal lease where the Town would own the assets at the end of the term. Mr. Pacheco further explained that the expense is the same is if it were purchased and what Enterprise provides is for the Town to not to have to pay for the full cost upfront. Enterprise would also assist the Town in acquiring the vehicles in its desired cycle. Mr. Pizzi joined the discussion and directed Finance Director Parchment to approach the Council and answer any questions

segs.head: - Discussion and Action of the Town of Medley Medical Bathing Services Program.
segs.text: - Discussion and Action of the Town of Medley Medical Bathing Services Program. Mayor Martell addressed the item and stated that the bathing services should be provided by medical health care providers opposed to being funded by the Town. Thus, the Mayor recommended to end the program and advise the current participants to obtain the services from their health care providers. Mayor Martell also explained that said program, in accordance with the Town attorney s legal opinion, should be funded from the Town of Medley foundation instead of the general funds and said services can be obtained from the individual s medical provider. Director Lizmari Valido joined the discussion and stated that the program currently has five participants for an estimated cost of thirteen thousand dollars per year. Additionally, she noted that the service is being provided to individuals who truly need it and are in a vulnerable state, thus changing the service provider would be difficult and uncomfortable for them. Vice Mayor Ayala expressed his disagreement with the cancellation of the program and explained that it will change the public opinion of the mayor if the proposal is approved. After a brief discussion Councilperson Pacheco made a motion as follows, TO CONTINUE WITH THE EXISTING FIVE (5) PARTICIPANTS OF THE MEDICAL BATHING PROGRAM FUNDED BY THE TOWN OF MEDLEY FOUNDATION AND TO END THE PROGRAM MOVING FORWARD FOR FUTURE APPLICANTS. votes: Councilwoman Ayala made a motion as follows, TO REMOVE THE ANNUAL POVERTY INCOME GUIDELINES FROM THE SPORTS CONTRIBUTION PROGRAM AND TO FUND THE SPORTS CONTRIBUTION PROGRAM WITH TOWN OF MEDLEY FOUNDATION FUNDING. Councilperson Pacheco seconded the motion, and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Policy and Procedures of the Sports Contribution Program. Councilwoman Ayala addressed the item and requested for the income constraints implemented for the sports contribution program be removed. Councilwoman Ayala also stated that since the March meeting three applications had been received and rejected due to the income limitation put in effect. Additionally, she explained that the complaints she has received are a repercussion of making rushed decisions and how implemented policies at times do not work in all circumstances. Once more she proposed to have the income-based qualification for the program removed. Councilwoman Ayala further stated that the Council, as members of the Town of Medley Foundation, could meet in a quarterly basis to address and recruit funding for the foundation. Mayor Martell reiterated the Town attorney s legal opinion about funding these programs though the Town of Medley Foundation and stated the importance of reaching out to businesses for donations. It was the consensus of the Town Council to approve the recent rejected applications submitted for the sport contribution program. Without further discussion, Councilwoman Ayala made a motion as follows, TO REMOVE THE ANNUAL POVERTY INCOME GUIDELINES FROM THE SPORTS CONTRIBUTION PROGRAM AND TO FUND THE SPORTS CONTRIBUTION PROGRAM WITH TOWN OF MEDLEY FOUNDATION FUNDING. segs.head: - Discussion and Action on the Town of Medley Community Pool Operations.
votes: Mayor Martell placed a motion to adjourn the meeting. The motion was carried unanimously, and the meeting was adjourned at 5:20 pm.
segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Town of Medley Community Pool Operations. Town Attorney Pizzi clarified that the Town received a bid for the community pool management services, and a brief presentation had previously been given to the Council by the vendor that had been selected. Therefore, the first part presented a resolution awarding the bid to the selected contractor. Mayor Martell then explained the proposed operations for the community pool and stated the proposed hours of operation which were announced to be Fridays from 1:00pm to 7:00pm, Saturdays and Sundays from 10:00am to 7:00pm. Moreover, Mayor Martell explained that the Town hired a company for maintenance of the pool therefore the language needs to be adjusted on proposal to remove the maintenance component. Mayor Martell also announced the groundbreaking event for the community pool which was stated to be the first Saturday in June, with an opening date to the public that Friday June 2, 2023. Additionally, it was explained that the community pool open season will begin the second week of May until the second week of September. Furthermore, it was explained that hours would need to be added on the proposal to accommodate the scheduling from Social Services and Parks and Recreational director Lizmari Valido for the summer camp, and the Medley Youth Social Club (MYSC) summer activities. segs.head: - Presentation of Award by Cigna to the Town of Medley for Long-Term Partnership.
votes: Councilperson Pacheco placed a motion as follows, TO APPROVE THE RENEWAL OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY COMMERCIAL INSURANCE POLICIES AND APPROVE THE RENEWAL OF THE TOWN OF MEDLEY EMPLOYEE MEDICAL BENEFIT INSURANCE POLICY. Mayor Martell seconded the motion, and it carried unanimously.
segs.text: - Presentation of Award by Cigna to the Town of Medley for Long-Term Partnership. Jennifer Gambill, client advisor, Lissette Calderon, accounts benefit executive, Ted Konstantopoulos, regional growth leader for employee benefits, and Allison Velilla account executive for commercial property casualty with Morris and Reynolds a division of World Insurance Associates LLC approached the Council. Mrs. Gambill then announced that Morris and Reynolds have merged with World Insurance Associates, LLC and informed the Council that after thirty years of working with the Town of Medley Mr. Bob Reynolds has retired, therefore he chose her to be his replacement to work alongside the Town. It was expressed how the Town has reached an amazing outcome during this year s negotiations due to the combined efforts of staff and the Mayor resulting in a zero increase to the Cigna healthcare to both the Town and employees as well as a zero-cost increase to any of the Town s employee benefits despite a small increase in the employee assistance program of $175.00. Additionally, it was noted that the Towns five-year average for increases is seven percent better than the rest of the industry nationwide which is a testament to the Town s well managed plan. Workers Compensation claims have decreased which is a positive result supported by the Town proactive approach to safety and loss control. segs.head: - Resolution C-2120 Approving an Urban Qualification Agreement for Participation In the Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) and Home Investment Partnership Program Funds with Miami-Dade County for Fiscal Years 2024, 2025, and 2026; Authorizing the Town Mayor to Execute the Agreement and any Attachments as Required by Miami-Dade County; Providing for Implementation; and Providing for an Effective Date.
votes: Councilperson Pacheco placed a motion to approve Resolution C-2120. Vice-Mayor Ayala seconded the motion, and it carried unanimously.
segs.text: - Resolution C-2120 Approving an Urban Qualification Agreement for Participation In the Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) and Home Investment Partnership Program Funds with Miami-Dade County for Fiscal Years 2024, 2025, and 2026; Authorizing the Town Mayor to Execute the Agreement and any Attachments as Required by Miami-Dade County; Providing for Implementation; and Providing for an Effective Date. Councilwoman Rodriguez addressed the Town Attorney for clarification on this item. Town Attorney Michael Pizzi then explained that the federal government HUD has millions of dollars in block grants that are made available, and municipalities must go through the State or County government to apply for those grants. One grant is the (CDBG) block grant which provides federal funds for home improvements, affordable housing, public facilities, and homeowner assistance programs. Therefore, the County received funds of over millions of dollars for these programs, and by the Town signing the interlocal agreement, it will be eligible from 2024 through 2026 to put in applications to receive funding for projects that assist residents. Vice-Mayor Ayala joined the discussion and stated that this item would also be a matter of discussion for his add-on Town of Medley item. Councilperson Pacheco placed a motion to approve Resolution C-2120. Vice-Mayor Ayala seconded the motion, and it carried unanimously.

votes: Mayor Martell placed a motion to approve Resolution C-2123. Councilperson Pacheco seconded the motion, and the votes were cast as follows, Mayor Roberto Martell- Yes Vice-Mayor Edgar Ayala- No Councilmember Lizelh Ayala- No Councilmember Karina Pacheco- Yes Councilmember Ivan Pacheco- Yes The motion was carried by majority of vote.
segs.text: - Resolution C-2123 Appointing Michael Salem as the Deputy Director and Executive Assistant to the Town of Medley Social Services and Parks and Recreations Department; Providing for Implementation; and Providing for an Effective Date. Michael Pizzi announced a change to the Resolution presented which said language will now state Resolution appointing Michael Salem as Assistant to the Town of Medley Social Services and Parks and Recreations Department . Town Clerk Victoria Martinez acknowledged the changes made. Councilwoman Rodriguez expressed that the administration has been disrespectful in hiring employees, who have already begun working, and bringing Resolutions months later for ratification and approval by the Council after the fact. Additionally, she stated that there is no Resolution or legislation in the Town that allows for this process and reiterated how disrespectful it is. Councilwoman Rodriguez further stated that as elected officials the administration should not bypass the appointment of staff and exclude them from the process which is both unethical and against the democratic process. Therefore, Councilwoman Rodriguez expressed her disagreement, and that she will not support the item. segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Appointment of One (1) Full-Time Meal Program Driver/Helper/Attendant for the Town of Medley Hot Meal Department. Director of the Hot Meal Program Fatima Fuentes approached the Council and recommended to hire Fabian Emilio Estevez Gonzalez Funes. Councilperson Pacheco began the discussion by stating that the applicant does not show to have any food handling qualifications and that the applicant is new to the country, not bilingual or has experience in this field. Additionally, Councilperson Pacheco stated that the Council had discussed at the previous executive session and had agreed to start hiring experienced individuals. Thus, he expressed his disagreement with the recommendation. Councilwoman Pacheco reiterated the comments expressed by Councilperson Pacheco and emphasized on the bilingual requirement for hire of the position. Director Fuentes stated that the program consists of employees who do not speak the English language and receive their certifications after being hired. In addition, Director Fuentes stated that she could not select another individual, because the requirements were not met by any of the other applicants. Without further discussion, Mayor Martell placed a motion to hire Director Fuentes recommended applicant. The motion was not seconded, therefore it died. segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Appointment of Three (3) Police Officer Positions for the Town of Medley Police Department. segs.text: - Presentation by Councilwoman Rodriguez in Collaboration with the University of Miami DAWN Alzheimer s Research Team: Empowering the Community Through Education and Advancing Understanding Through Genetic Research. Vanessa Rodriguez, BA, Research Manager residing at 1810 W 56 ST Hialeah, FL 33012 and Karina Celis, MD, Scientific Associate residing at 2511 SW 26 Lane Miami, Florida 33133 from the DAWN Alzheimer s research team at the University of Miami School of Medicine approached the Council and gave a brief overview of their initiative and proposed partnership with the Town of Medley to host a community event to spread Alzheimer awareness and recruit participants for their genetic research study. segs.text: - Resolution C-2209 Approving a Services Agreement between the Town of Medley and Atlantic Swim School for Aquatic Facility Maintenance Services for the Town of Medley Community Pool; Providing for Implementation; and Providing for an Effective Date. Attorney Pizzi began the discussion by explaining that the Town has been paying a company solely for the maintenance service of the community pool, but they have failed to efficiently regulate pool chemicals resulting in the Town receiving a citation. Thus, staff now recommends that the pool maintenance services be provided by the same company that provides the Town s lifeguard operational services. Councilwoman Lizelh Rodriguez stated that any time something occurs which can cause a public hazard, the Mayor and Council should be informed immediately in addition to be publicly noticed. Vice-Mayor Jinete expressed concerns with the proposed estimate and asked if the price could still be negotiated. After a brief discussion, Vice-Mayor Jinete placed a motion as follows, TO AUTHORIZE THE MAYOR TO MEET WITH LEGAL AND NEGOTIATE A FINAL CONTRACT WITH ATLANTIS SWIM SCHOOL FOR AQUATIC FACILITY MAINTENANCE SERVICES BEFORE BRINGING THE MATTER BACK TO COUNCIL BUT ALLOW ATLANTIS SWIM SCHOOL TO ASSUME TEMPORARY SERVICE OF THE COMMUNITY POOL FOR THE PRICE | PRESENTED. segs.head: - Discussion and Action on the Renewal of the Town of Medley Employee Benefits Insurance Policy.
votes: Vice-Mayor Jinete placed a motion as follows, TO RENEW THE HEALTH INSURANCE BENFIT WITH CIGNA AND ACCEPT THE NINE PERCENT (9%) INCREASE FOR THE 2025 YEAR. Councilmember Ayala seconded the motion, and the motion was carried unanimously.
segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Renewal of the Town of Medley Employee Benefits Insurance Policy. Jennifer Gambil with World s Insurance approached the Council and explained the organization s long term historical partnership with the Town. Ms. Gambil continued to state that the Town has expressed how Cigna has provided excellent customer care to the employees. The loss ratio on medical insurance was explained which was said to be at 112% and how the 2024 renewal had no increase to the Town s plan rates. Nonetheless, it was explained that for the 2025 year the Town is left with two options, a (9%) increase to the insurance policy to keep the current benefits as status quo for the employees, and the alternative option of a (3.5%) renewal rate increasing employee deductibles, medical co-payments, and prescription costs. After a brief discussion on the matter, it was agreed upon to keep the status quo on all benefits, thus the Town to accept the 9% increase option totaling to a $216,000.00 increase. Vice-Mayor Jinete placed a motion as follows, TO RENEW THE HEALTH INSURANCE BENFIT WITH CIGNA AND ACCEPT THE NINE PERCENT (9%) INCREASE FOR THE 2025 YEAR. Councilmember Ayala seconded the motion, and the motion was carried unanimously.

segs.head: - Update and Discussion on New Federal Overtime Regulations.
votes: Vice-Mayor Jinete placed a motion to adjourn, and it was carried unanimously.
segs.text: - Update and Discussion on New Federal Overtime Regulations. Town Attorney Michael Pizzi stated that under the fair labor act anyone that works over 40 hours is required to get overtime. The only exemption to getting overtime is if your classified in an executive position. Attorney Pizzi further stated that effective January 28, 2025 a law goes into effect mandating that if an employee is making below $58,000.00 a year regardless of employee s classification, they would be required to receive overtime. Thus, the Attorney s recommendation is that the Mayor, Town Attorney, and Finance Department have a meeting to keep up with the status of this legislation and see what impact it would have to the Town. Moreover, return the item to Council if there is a need for direction or change. Without further discussion, Vice-Mayor Jinete placed a motion to adjourn, and it was carried unanimously. Councilwoman Rodriguez inquired about the proposed resurfacing of the NW 68" Court and NW 68" Place area and stated whether or not it could possibly include drainage improvements to alleviate flooding issues in the area. segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Appointment of Child Care Attendant Positions for the Town of Medley Social Services and Parks and Recreation Department. segs.text: - Request by Mayor Martell for Discussion and Action on the Proposed Declaration of Certain Real Property Owned by the Town of Medley as Surplus Property. Mayor Martell explained that afer assessing the details of the property and speaking with staff, he would like to revisit the matter and put the property for sale. Vice-Mayor Ayala inquired about the Mayor s need for the sale of the property. Mayor Martell explained that after the Council s decision to expand the hours of operations of the community pool and the budget issues it creates, the revenue from the sale of this property can help fund the operations and the budget gap. Town attorney Michael Pizzi clarified and further explained that the matter at hand is not being considered for action to sell the property rather than for the Council to authorize staff, upon approval of the Town Council, to bid the property which would then give the Council full authority to consider whether it is desired to sell the property. Councilperson Pacheco stated that he has supported the sale of Town property in the past with the goal to achieve funding sources for Town road and drainage projects that are very much needed in areas such as the Lakeside Retirement Park. Councilman Pacheco further stated that the extension of community pool hours of operation is another financial concern that needs to be resolved, hence his support for the sale of the property. Vice-Mayor Ayala stated that this item is presented with the waiver of the RFP process due to its urgency and for emergency purposes, but he continues to urge the Council to follow the correct procurement and RFP process. Jorge Soto Director of the Water and Sewer Department approached the Council and explained that this service was put out for competitive bidding by Miami Beach and the Town is proposing to piggyback off its procurement process. Director Soto continued to explain that for the bidding purpose, interested companies will need to take apart the motors to determine the amounts for their bid submittal, thus making it a complicated process. Vice-Mayor Ayala reiterated that although he supports Director Soto in this initiative, he urges the Town to responsibly follow the Town s procurement process. Therefore, he proposed to approve this item for a shorter period to allow for the Town to put out a request for proposal and follow the correct procurement protocols. segs.head: - Request by Councilmember Pacheco for Discussion and Action on the Implementation of Wage Ranges for all Town of Medley Non-Bargaining Positions.
segs.text: - Request by Councilmember Pacheco for Discussion and Action on the Implementation of Wage Ranges for all Town of Medley Non-Bargaining Positions. Councilperson Pacheco expressed his intent to have a pay scale established for all Town of Medley employees. Mayor then recommended a workshop for the further discussion on this item once numbers are gathered. Councilwoman Rodriguez expressed her concern with this matter and stated that setting salary wages and scales should be done by a third-party expertise and that the common practice is for this task to be done by a consulting firm. Hence, she suggested the Town to contract a consultant firm so that the process can be done completely unbiased. Mayor Martell stated that the Council will be setting the wage scales, and Councilwoman Rodriguez reiterated that it should be performed by a professional. Without further discussion, Councilperson Pacheco placed a motion as follows, MOTION TO DIRECT THE TOWN ATTORNEY AND FINANCE DIRECTOR TO CREATE A PAY SCALE FOR ALL TOWN OF MEDLEY EMPLOYEES, AND PRESENT THE NUMBERS IN THE FORM OF A COUNCIL WORKSHOP FOR DISCUSSION AND ACTION Mayor Martell seconded the motion, and the votes were cast as follows, Mayor Roberto Martell- Yes Vice-Mayor Edgar Ayala- Yes Councilmember Lizelh Rodriguez- No Councilmember Karina Pacheco- Yes Councilmember Ivan Pacheco- Yes The motion passed by majority of vote.

segs.text: - Discussion and Action Request to Retain Five (5) Consultants for Child Care Attendant Positions for the Social Services and Parks and Recreation Department. Councilwoman Rodriguez asked for clarification on the intent to hire consultants. It was explained that the Town would hire independent employees that would perform the same duties, but they would be 1099 employees like the current tutor. segs.text: - Finance Director Report on the Town of Medley Community Pool. Finance Director Charmaine Parchment approached the Council and stated that she has received the cost associated with adjusting the community pool opening hours as requested in the December Council meeting. Ms. Parchment further stated that from March 1** to November 2024, the cost estimate is $109,950 and that $50,000 budgeted is already budgeted for the summer, leaving a shortage of approximately $ 60,000. Director Parchment requested direction on the allocations to budget the needed funding for this directive. Councilwoman Rodriguez asked for a monthly breakdown, and it was stated that from March to June 2024 the cost is quoted at $41,600, from July to September 2024 is $47,200, and lastly $ 21,150 for October 1 to November 24, 2024. It was noted that the last range of October through November would fall into the 2024/2025 fiscal year s budget, therefore the Town only needs to budget funds for the remaining $44,400. segs.head: - Discussion on the Proposed Budget for the Fiscal Year October 1, 2024, through September 30, 2025.
segs.text: - Discussion on the Proposed Budget for the Fiscal Year October 1, 2024, through September 30, 2025. Town Attorney Pizzi began the discussion and explained that the millage rate to be set by the Council tonight would preliminarily cap that number. Thus, the Council could set a lower rate but cannot go past the preliminary millage rate. Finance Director Charmaine Parchment discussed the Town s preliminary 2024-2025 budget and announced the 2024 certified taxable property value to be $5,795,357,513 which reflects an increase of $602,757,161 in taxable property value. Director Parchment further stated that the recommended millage rate for fiscal year 2024-2025 is 3.2 mills per $1,000 and reiterated that the millage rate can be lowered but not set any higher than the preliminary millage rate. Additionally, director Parchment stated a gross tax revenue of $2,967.342. Director Parchment also discussed the preliminary 2024-2025 general fund s revenues and expenses, as well as the budget timeline for fiscal year 2024-2025. Director Parchment further informed the Council that a final budget recommendation will be given prior to the first budget hearing in September. Town Clerk Victoria Martinez announced that the first budget public hearing is scheduled to be held on Tuesday September 10, 2024 at 6:00 pm and the second and last public hearing is scheduled for Tuesday September 24, 2024, also at 6:00 pm. segs.head: - Discussion and Action on the Appointment of One (1) Full-Time Economic Development Coordinator Position(Reclassification) for the Capital Improvement Projects Department.
votes: Vice Mayor Ayala placed a motion as follows, "TO APPOINT MICHAEL SALEM TO THE POSITION OF FULL-TIME ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT COORDINATOR FOR THE CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PROJECTS DEPARTMENT" Mayor Martell seconded the motion, and the motion was carried unanimously.
segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Appointment of One (1) Full-Time Economic Development Coordinator Position(Reclassification) for the Capital Improvement Projects Department. Town Attorney Pizzi stated that the Social Services and Parks and Recreation department just received approval to hire a coordinator and no longer needs the services Mr. Michael Salem's provides for the department. Mr. Pizzi continued to state that Mr. Salem is currently assisting multiple departments with his many years of experience,therefore proving to be an asset by other means for the Town. Thus,to fit an accurate job description for the work Mr. Salem is currently doing for the Town,the recommendation is to appoint Mr. Salem to the position of economic development coordinator. Vice Mayor Ayala noted that this matter contradicts the process that has been established for the addition of items to the agenda, and that the item did not include any backup documentation. Vice-Mayor Ayala encouraged the administration to correct this method. It was clarified that Mr. Salem would no longer have the title of assistant to the social services and parks and recreation department. Vice Mayor Ayala placed a motion as follows, "TO APPOINT MICHAEL SALEM TO THE POSITION OF FULL-TIME ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT COORDINATOR FOR THE CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PROJECTS DEPARTMENT" Mayor Martell seconded the motion, and the motion was carried unanimously.

votes: Mayor Martell placed a motion as follows, "TO INSTRUCT THE LEGAL AND POLICE DEPARTMENT TO LOOK INTO THE ABILITY TO IMPLEMENT A POLICY TO PROHIBIT CARRYING FIREARMS WITHIN THE LAKESIDE RETIREMENT PARK RECREATIONAL CENTER" Councilwoman Pacheco seconded the motion, and the motion was carried unanimously.
segs.text: - Request by Councilperson Pacheco for Discussion and Action on Public Safety and Prohibition to Carry Firearms at the Town of Medley Lakeside Retirement Park. Councilperson Pacheco stated that his intent is to prohibit firearms from being entered into the Lakeside Retirement Home Recreational Center. Vice-Mayor Ayala asked if the proposal by councilmen Pacheco can legally be done. Chief Jeanette Said-Jinete approached the Council and clarified that the proposed item requires legal review to confirm that the Town would not violate citizen's second amendment right to carry. Attorney Pizzi explained that the state of Florida has become a constitutional carry state and municipalities have constrained ability to restrict the carrying of firearms. After a brief discussion, Mayor Martell placed a motion as follows, "TO INSTRUCT THE LEGAL AND POLICE DEPARTMENT TO LOOK INTO THE ABILITY TO IMPLEMENT A POLICY TO PROHIBIT CARRYING FIREARMS WITHIN THE LAKESIDE RETIREMENT PARK RECREATIONAL CENTER" Councilwoman Pacheco seconded the motion, and the motion was carried unanimously.

segs.text: - Discussion and Action on the Town of Medley Hot Meal Program. Finance Director Charmain Parchment approached the Council and began her presentation on the Town of Medley hot meal program addressing the cost of the same and the finance impact of the proposed price increase. Ms. Parchment explained that the hot meal program was budgeted for $770,000 for FY 23/24 at a current rate of $7.70 per meal and that the proposed rate of $8.64 per meal would create a shortfall of $69,000 for the period of March 23, 2024, to September 30", 2024. Ms. Parchment further presented the options to fund the shortfall, which included using unused department funds, using the surplus from the current fiscal year, or with the Council s approval, a grant from the Town of Medley foundation, and lastly, a combination of any of the presented options. The presentation was translated into the Spanish language for the Spanish speaking members of the public in attendance. Councilperson Pacheco began the discussion and explained what occurred at the March 13, 2024 special Council meeting, stating that he placed a motion approving the renewal of the contract, but the motion that passed was to hold a Council workshop to further discuss the matter, which since then, could not occur because the supplier sent an email to cut off all services to the Town. Mayor Martell announced that he would recuse himself from the discussion and action on this matter due to a conflict of interest. Therefore, Attorney Pizzi explained that the third district court of appeal issued an opinion related to this instance in which to hold quorum the Town Council needs to have three voting members. However, in the instance where there is a total of three elected officials, and one recuses the body loses quorum. Attorney Pizzi further stated that given the circumstances, this matter could no longer be addressed and would be tabled for another meeting of the Town Council. It was also clarified that the position was to remain open.

segs.text: - Request by Councilwoman Rodriguez for Discussion and Action on Public Meetings: Protocols and Decorum. Councilwoman Rodriguez began the discussion by addressing the memorandum circulated to the Council in reference to public meetings, protocols, and decorum. Councilwoman then continued to read the memorandum into the record as follows, The purpose of this memorandum is to express my deep concern with the format in which public meetings have been taking place. At the most recent council meeting on February 21, 2024, we witnessed the unprofessionalism in its highest form and a violation of our right to speak as elected officials. By limiting the legislative body from having on-going discussions is a violation of our rights as elected officials. Most importantly, it infringes on our First Amendment rights. As someone who loves this county and honors the sacrifices of our founding fathers, I will not continue to tolerate this behavior, which has only worsened since I joined this council in November 2020. The practice of limiting open discussions in public meetings is a threat to the democratic process that makes the United States the great nation that it is. I encourage this administration to honor the oath we took and stop this practice as it is detrimental to the duties of an elected official. segs.text: - Presentation on"Freebee Medley"Program Proposal Claudia Miro, Business Development and Government Affairs representative with Freebie and with office located at 371 NE 61 Street Miami approached the Council and gave a brief presentation of the on-demand transportation services and what it can offer to the Town as a micro transit door to door service. It was emphasized that the Freebie transportation services can be personalized based on the residential populations needs. Additionally, it was noted that grant funding by the Florida Department of Transportation (FDOT) has been awarded to the Town of Medley for services such as Freebie to offset the costs for the first three years. It was also noted that the desired wait time would determine the amount of vehicles needed, thus the overall cost for the services. Ms. Miro also stated that due to the grant fund disbursement schedule, it was suggested to initiate the program in July, with an estimated total cost of$100,000.00 per year for which the FDOT grant would cover 50% of the expense totaling to about $50,000 to the Town. segs.text: - Resolution Approving a State-Funded Grant Agreement with the Florida Department of Transportation (FDOT) for Participation in Funding for On-Demand Transportation Services; Authorizing the Town Mayor to Execute the Grant Agreement with FDOT; Providing for Implementation; and Providing for an Effective Date. Town Attorney Pizzi explained that the proposed item is for the approval to receive a grant of $132,000 to support the Freebie on-demand transportation program. It was noted that this is a matching grant, therefore the Town must match 50% which the Town has agreed to do with CITT funding as well as other donations received from business like Waste Management. Mayor Stefano expressed concerns with the boundaries of the Freebie transportation program. Attorney Pizzi informed the Council that the Town will discuss with Freebie the expansion of limits to frequently visited locations by the residents, such as the local Walmart, or a commonly visited medical clinic. Councilperson Ayala stated that the Town previously provided transportation services that many residents benefitted and preferred using. It was clarified that the Town is currently using alternative transportation services to assist residents. Vice-Mayor Jinete made a motion to approve Resolution C-2202. Mayor Stefano seconded the motion, and the motion was carried unanimously.

segs.text: - Discussion and Action on Town of Medley Police Department Re-Classifications. Chief Young approached the Council and announced the following reclassifications within the Police department. segs.text: * Michael Salem - Grants / Economic Development Coordinator Capengineerin: Executive Summary C.A.P. Engineering, Inc. (CAP) was charged with the responsibility to work closely with the Town of Medley CIP Department to review and assess the progress of on-going and new projects with an emphasis on those that have grants. We were to schedule and provide recommendations, and to revise prioritization schedules, as necessary. CAP reviewed all the available documents and assessed the status of each project, this included: project progress, reporting, extensions, progress of achievements to date, identification of problems, and other issues. Our goal remains to provide engineering support, project management, restructuring of project priorities, troubleshooting, and other technical assistance. CAP is to support engineers, contractors and other stakeholders, as may be needed to ensure timely completion of all projects. Upon completion of the review, CAP found that the current schedule prioritization is based on grant projects which we highly recommend. CAP was instrumental in enhancing current levels of documentation to ensure timely compliance and achievements of each project goals. All current projects are up to date and moving forward towards timely completion. Town Attorney Pizzi began the discussion by explaining that the state of Florida passed the Live Local Act to address the affordable housing crisis which allowed developers to build and bypass the city processes with the condition that 60% of the dwellings be dedicated to workforce housing. Therefore, concurrent with Miami Dade rapid transit zones Miami-Dade County has negotiated agreements with developers to allow them to build multifaceted mixed-use buildings to be located near the palmetto metro station and the other near the animal shelter center in Medley. Mr. Pizzi continued to explain that he has met with the developers to discuss the matter, and they have agreed to assist the Town with its needs and that although the developers do not have to provide permits to the Town, the Town will still provide police and water services as well as zoning, planning and code enforcement services. In addition, Mr. Pizzi stated that said developers have agreed to not overwhelm the Town s social services programs and that they will pay for services such as water and any utilities upgrades that may be needed.
